result.summary:
WP-36: fixed all 7 open findings from w3-s2-minors-continue.json. The major finding reproduced with the reviewer probe (cases a-e). Every probe case passes now.

F1 (major, overlay/merge.go): the root cause was that mergeMap read the object's dispatch while an overlay composite stood in for a base scalar. merge() later put that scalar back when the composite held nothing but removals.
- New flow: the first pass leaves every replaced base value in place. Then a new `settle` step decides which base scalars stay before `static.Select` reads the dispatch.
- settle first puts all such overlay composites in at once. If the dispatch is unchanged, no mix of them can change it (a composite fails every rule that tests its member), so nothing else is done.
- Otherwise each overlay value is normalized on a `Clone()`, under the member's schema in the dispatch the base scalars give, with diagnostics turned off (new `applier.quiet`). A value of which something remains stands in; one holding only removals leaves the base scalar.
- settle does nothing once the diagnostic budget is spent. Its cost is at most the merge of the same values, so the merge stays linear.
- The assumption is pinned by the new TestDispatchMembersFixed (no branch of the rendered schema changes the schema of a member its rules test). A synthetic schema shows the check can fail.

Class members, each with its own test, all failing on the pre-change code:
- (a) a base $patch inside the document stays data, flat and nested {x:{y:null}}
- (b) a map list still merges by key
- (c) a delete entry still deletes
- (d) the document is still replaced whole
- (e) a boolean dispatch member, a string dispatch member, and a dispatch member of a nested object (synthetic schema)
- a second base scalar replaced beside the dispatch member
- a dispatch member with a structured schema (new fixedDispatch schema)

Negatives: a value {a:1} or a written list replaces the type and clears the dispatch; a cleared dispatch replaces a map list whole; removals over a base composite leave it; a misplaced $patch inside a type value is reported once (object and list cases); a free-content $patch is misplaced under a cleared dispatch.

Same-class fix for the related location: dispatchPos used to name the first overlay member a rule tests, even one that changed nothing. It now names the first such member whose member the merge actually changed (removed, added, given another scalar, or replaced by what remains of a composite), in overlay order, else the overlay object. TestRedispatchRelated covers each member that changes nothing (an equal scalar, a null for an absent member, a flat or nested removal-only value, a composite over a composite of the same or another kind), each member that changes something, the order rule, and a value without a position. It replaces TestDispatchPos.

Fuzz and budget:
- FuzzOverlay has a new metamorphic property (dropRemovals): removing an overlay member whose value is a null tree and whose base value is a scalar changes neither the result nor the diagnostics. It skips $patch members, the ruralz.io/patch annotation and document positions in either view. Seeds a-d plus one value case were added.
- New budget row (misplaced $patch in values replacing base scalars) and TestSettleAfterBudget.
- Comments were rewritten for mergeMap, pendingMember, exemptHolders, the package doc and the TestDispatchTestsScalars rationale.

Minor 2: redispatched now reports CodeBasePatch (RZ-CFG-006), as 01 req 25 and its 006 test-plan row require. Message, hint and related location are unchanged. Updated the CodeSchema/CodeBasePatch comments, the package and Apply docs, and the expected strings in TestRedispatchedBasePatch, TestRedispatchNested, TestUnresolvedDispatch and the budget row.

Minor 3: rewrote the TestCredentialWarnings comment to match walker.literal (wording in the 013 contract request below). Added the row "${A}${B:-; }" (A set, B unset, no warning). It kills an "every expression must be sourced" mutant.

Minor 4: added rows "key${A};" (warns; kills the reviewer's S5 mutant `return true`) and its mirror ";${A}key". Added FuzzSubst seeds "key${A};", "0${A} " and "${A}${B:-; }"; seeds #18 and #19 now kill S5 without fuzzing.

Minor 5: the walk.go literal doc now says a value an error left unresolved is still read there, its undefined variables taking their text from no source, and warn then drops the warning.

Minor 6: the subst.go package doc and the TestAuthoredReading doc now state the exception: detectors read authored runs only; the header literal rule also reads whether each expression takes its text from the variable source or from a default. New rows pin "${A:-;}" with A empty (warns) and A set (no warning).

Minor 7: rewrapped the package-doc paragraph ("the text substitution writes is bounded by Options.MaxOutputBytes for the whole render") and the broken MaxDiagnostics sentence.

Round-3 summary correction for the record: headerValue warns when an authored run holds text other than framing, or when no expression takes its text from the variable source. It does not warn "unless every expression resolved from the source", as the round-3 summary said.

contractRequests: Spec 01 owner, 01 J row 013 ('a headers set[].value literal'): record the reading the code implements, replacing the round-3 summary's wording 'warns unless every expression resolved from the source'. The credential detectors read only the authored runs of a scalar: its literal text and every ${NAME:-default} default, taken or not, cut at each ${NAME} without default. They never read a variable's value, so their result never depends on the Environment. A credential header set[].value (authorization, proxy-authorization, cookie, x-api-key) is a literal, RZ-CFG-013, when it is non-empty and either an authored run holds text other than framing, or no expression takes its text from the variable source. Framing is a leading Bearer or Basic scheme of the first run, in any case, or text holding no letter or digit. A default an unset or empty variable takes is not the source. So this rule depends on which variables the Environment sets: '${A:-;}' warns when A is unset or empty and not when A is set; '${X:-hunter2}' warns whether X is set or not; '${A}${B:-; }' with A set does not warn; 'key${A};' warns.

Spec 01 owner, OQ against 01 req 25 and 27 (unresolved dispatch, filed earlier; restated with the codes now emitted). A Policy spec.type holding ${VAR} selects no branch at stage D. Three consequences follow: (1) config's composite members merge as free content, so an overlay $patch inside them is RZ-CFG-005; (2) CheckBase reads a base config.schema there as outside a document, so a base $patch there is RZ-CFG-006; (3) an overlay that sets the spec.type of a base validation.json-schema Policy to an expression moves the base config.schema out of the document position, so a base $patch there is RZ-CFG-006, related the overlay type. It was RZ-CFG-005 before this round. Withdraw any earlier statement that names RZ-CFG-005 for a redispatched base $patch: the code now follows 01 req 25 ('$patch in a base document: RZ-CFG-006').

Spec 01 owner, 01 req 25 (record the decision, no code change needed): an overlay composite that replaces a base scalar and holds nothing but removals (null members, $patch: delete entries, at any depth) leaves the base scalar in place, and the merge reads the object's if/then dispatch from that result. A Policy spec.type the overlay writes as {a: null} therefore stays the base type, and config merges under it. The related location of a redispatch diagnostic is the first overlay member a dispatch rule tests whose member the merge changed, else the overlay object.
deviations: merge.go: dispatchPos now takes the overlay object and the index of the member that changed the dispatch, instead of the schema and the overlay object. That index is found during the merge. TestDispatchPos is replaced by the merge-level TestRedispatchRelated.

settle normalizes a copy of each overlay value that replaces a base scalar, but only when standing those values in changes the dispatch, and never once the diagnostic budget is spent. That costs at most one extra normalize per such value, so the merge stays linear. The work runs before the budget is reached, so an object with a replaced dispatch member and many other replaced scalars allocates in proportion to its input. The budget rows cover only the no-decider case.

result.summary:
WP-35 round-3 findings: all 9 fixed. Each was reproduced before any code change, and each fix has a test that fails on the pre-change code (overlay of the snapshot in scratchpad wp35r4/before) or kills a mutant.

1. MAJOR, cap overflow (mapping.go). newMapper now sets keep = min(max(limit,1), math.MaxInt-1)+1. record prunes on `len(m.out)-m.keep >= m.keep`, which cannot wrap. Class members:
- keep+1 overflowing at math.MaxInt
- 2*keep wrapping from math.MaxInt/2 up
- the same arithmetic in defaults/keep.go and canonical/keep.go, filed as a contract request.
The Options.MaxDiagnostics doc now states the clamp.
Tests: caps MaxInt/2-1, MaxInt/2, MaxInt/2+1, MaxInt-1 and MaxInt were added to TestTruncationDeterministic and TestMaxDiagnosticsOption (plus math.MinInt). The new TestMapperKeep checks keep and that no prune happens. FuzzValidate gained a property that caps MaxInt and MaxInt/2 equal Validate. On the old code every one of these panics; two arithmetic mutants are each killed.

2. Uncharged long-text spans. Every span whose work grows with one text is now charged with its bytes right after it. Members:
- memo.intern: segment rendering and hashing, covering keyed keys, bare and quoted field names, depth-0 fields, and set elements
- every memo.scan, charged on work as well as counted in scanned
- the canonical JSON of duplicateKeys keys and of duplicateElements, plus the number literals it parses (itemJSONBytes/numberBytes)
- itemElem/elemBytes for number and object set elements, and the second ItemElem of a duplicate
- schemaidx.Walk's own work (walkUnits): two units per object member for its double dispatch, member-name bytes, keyed-entry member scans, element bytes
- the instance build: member-name hashing
- the validator span: nodes plus member-name and string bytes
- memo.index: compares of equal-length names, index-build key bytes, lookup bytes
- step lookups: children compared plus token bytes
- sortedNames: common-prefix bytes per comparison
- varsBelow: variable-name bytes
quote/shorten no longer scan the whole text (see 5). The Options.Yield doc was rewritten to list every unit and every span. TestYieldSchemaErrors, TestYieldCheckLists, TestYieldLocate, TestYieldVisit, TestInstance, TestNumberWorkBounded and TestYieldSortAndResult were updated. The new TestTextCharges has 23 per-member growth cases; 22 fail on the old code. The one that passes is the object set element, which was already charged.

3. MaxDiagnostics doc. It now says the cap bounds only the diagnostics kept and returned. Measured cost is about 0.5 KB per error in the validator and 1 KB per error in the mapping. It cites OQ-configuration-model-18 instead of 01 risk 1. The package doc was updated to match.

4. lcp memo size (paths.go). Each long segment now remembers its last compared sibling (lcpCache.peer). Only pairs whose common prefix reaches lcpMemo = 1 KiB go into memo.lcp, which therefore holds at most scanned/lcpMemo entries. TestLongSiblingPrefixes now asserts pairs*lcpMemo <= scanned and pairs <= doc/32. New cases cover descending order, medium (900-byte) names and 1 KiB names, and results with short paths are checked for sort order. The old memo fails the bound in 15 cases. TestCommonPrefixMemo was rewritten for the lcpMin/lcpMemo boundaries and peer eviction. Peer-cache and memo-lookup mutants are both killed.

5. quote/shorten. A new clip() reads at most maxQuoted runes. Output is identical to the []rune version: TestClipQuoteShorten compares the two, including invalid UTF-8. The uniqueness checks now reuse a pre-sized canonical JSON buffer. TestQuoteBoundedAlloc and TestLongTextAlloc fail on the old code: 5.0/7.0/8.6/10.6 bytes per document byte before, 1.0/3.0/2.0/2.0 now.

6. Duplicate keys. The validator's instance now keeps the first member, matching Get, locate and member. Class members fixed alongside:
- checkLists skips hidden member subtrees (built.shadowed, via ErrSkipChildren)
- checkReserved reports a repeated reserved key once
- varsBelow skips hidden values
TestDuplicateMemberFirstWins and TestShadowedMembersSkipped fail on the old code or under 4 mutants. schemaidx.AppendItemJSON (WP-03) still writes duplicate keys; filed as a contract request.

7. Missing segment kinds in TestLongSiblingPrefixes. Subtests were added for bare and quoted string set elements (duplicates) and for bare and quoted depth-0 unknown members. Two mutants that drop the cache for exactly those segment kinds are killed only by the new subtests.

8. Step index reads. step.find now returns the children it compared, and memo.step adds that to memo.read and charges it. The new TestStepIndex covers 0, 7, 8, 9 and 100 children. The no-index mutant is now killed by TestStepIndex and by TestLargeObjects (read 5,000,350,010 against a budget of 1,600,208). It used to pass in 73 s.

9. work.total doc reworded.

contractRequests: WP-37 (internal/config/defaults/keep.go:165) and WP-39 (internal/config/canonical/keep.go:127): the prune trigger `len(k.entries) >= 2*k.n` wraps negative for a cap n > math.MaxInt/2 (newKeeper keeps max(1, n)), so every append or offer prunes. Each prune sorts every entry and keeps all of them, which is quadratic in the diagnostics. Replace it with `len(k.entries)-k.n >= k.n` (canonical: `(!k.hasBound && len(k.entries) >= k.n) || len(k.entries)-k.n >= k.n`). Add caps math.MaxInt/2, math.MaxInt/2+1, math.MaxInt-1 and math.MaxInt to their cap tests, expecting the full result. Same class as WP-35 round-3 finding 1; WP-39's in-progress 'overflow-free arithmetic' task may already cover canonical.

WP-01 (internal/config/tree/tree.go, Node.Members and JSONValue): the contract does not say whether member keys are unique, and its methods disagree. Get and Set resolve the first member, while JSONValue keeps the last (m[mem.Key] assigned in member order). Proposed Members doc: '// Members are the object members in authored order (KindMap); keys are unique: a front end drops or reports a repeated key (profile/json.go, yaml.go). Code that meets a repeated key anyway resolves the first member, as Get does.' Also make JSONValue skip a key already in m, so it keeps the first. Stage F now resolves the first member everywhere it can. Without this statement, schemaidx.AppendItemJSON and ItemElem (WP-03) still write every member of a set element, so two set elements that are equal under first-wins can differ canonically. If WP-01 declines the uniqueness statement, WP-03 should make AppendItemJSON skip a member whose key an earlier member has, matching tree.Node.Get.
deviations: Finding 4: neither of the suggested fixes was used as given. Instead each long segment caches its last compared peer and its common-prefix length, and only pairs with a common prefix of at least 1 KiB go into the map. A plain 1 KiB threshold rescans medium prefixes on every comparison when many errors lie below two siblings, which is far over prefixBudget. Ranking siblings needs an order-maintenance structure because siblings arrive one at a time. The chosen design keeps scanned at or below 17.1 bytes per document byte across all cases and caps the map at one entry per 1,024 bytes scanned.
Finding 2, quote's scan: quote and shorten now read a bounded prefix instead of being charged for a full scan.

Finding 2, extra charges: the class was taken wider than the finding's list. The instance build's key hashing, the validator span's member-name and string bytes, memo.index byte charges, step-lookup token bytes, sortedNames prefix bytes, variable-name bytes and the number literals that canonical JSON parses are all charged too.

Finding 6, scope: the fix also covers checkLists (hidden member subtrees are skipped), checkReserved (a repeated reserved key is reported once) and varsBelow (hidden values are skipped), so that every check after the validator agrees with it.

Finding 3, optional part: the bound pre-check before building messages was not implemented. Most of the mapping's roughly 1 KB per error is locating the error, which the bound comparison needs anyway; the doc states the linear cost instead.
Finding 1, clamp value: the cap is clamped to math.MaxInt-1 rather than math.MaxInt/4, and the prune test is written so it cannot overflow; every cap below math.MaxInt is honoured exactly.

Finding 5, extra change: duplicateKeys and duplicateElements now reuse a canonical JSON buffer pre-sized to the scalar's length. Without it a long duplicate element allocated 6.5 bytes per document byte; with it, 2.0.

result.summary:
WP-37 round 4: I fixed all 13 round-3 findings at their root cause. Before changing code I reproduced F2, F3, F5, F6 and F7 on the pre-change snapshot (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp37r4/pre). Every fix and every class member has a test, and each test is proven by a mutation it kills: 99 of 99 mutants killed, run with /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp37r4/mutate.py and m_all.json in the same folder.

F1 (major, spoke rule untested). Added spoke_test.go. It builds a synthetic spoke, ruralz/v1test, with schemaidx.Load and NewSet: Route upstreams renamed backends, weight default 3, and the auth.api-key header member renamed hdr with default x-spoke. It adds a renaming spokeConverter. Cases: (a) lifecycle warnings use the spoke paths; (b) spoke defaults, including through the Policy config dispatch; (c) normalization uses the hub map list; (d) decode uses hub keyed paths and hub-declared config members; (e) Source.APIVersion is the spoke version while the tree and object carry the hub version; (f) a Run mixing both versions gives equal hub trees. Each of the 5 reviewer mutations is killed.

F3 (major, cap overflow). Class members: Stage.newWork keep/left, Run's newKeeper argument, and keeper.add's 2n threshold. Fix: keepOf(cap) = min(cap, MaxInt-1)+1, the same as schemaview and precedence; the prune test is now len-n >= n; Options.MaxDiagnostics documents this. Tests: TestHugeCaps (MaxInt, MaxInt-1, MaxInt/2, 1<<62, 1<<62-1, through Resource and Run with 1 and 2 workers) and TestKeeperPrunes (prunes ≤ adds/n+1 for every n, using a prunes counter).

F6 (major, invalid UTF-8). Normalize is now the gate for everything the canonical form cannot hold, in every tree including canonical content. A string or member name that is not valid UTF-8 is RZ-CFG-005 at its key-aware path and position, checked before scalar normalization; the message never shows the value. A number literal outside the RFC 8259 grammar is RZ-CFG-005 in canonical content too (only the range rule is waived there). A node of no JSON kind is RZ-CFG-005 as well. Tests: TestInvalidUTF8 with one exact row per position kind (typed string, map value, keyed key, set element, Duration, ByteSize, Decimal, plugin config, open config member, JSONSchemaDocument, below a secret field, member name, plugin member name), TestSubstitutedInvalidUTF8 (stage E then F then G), TestCanonicalNumberGrammar and TestNoJSONKind.

F2 (decode stopped at the first failure). The locator now walks the whole tree and reports every value that does not fit, up to the budget. The config decode runs even after a kind failure: the config type is the decoded spec.type, or the tree's when the kind struct was not decoded. Decode also runs after a normalization error, using only the locator, and skips nodes normalization already reported (the reported set holds at most the budget). The stack.path element names are now kept once computed, so many failures below one element stay linear. Tests: TestDecodeEveryFailure (two weights, two credentials, kind plus config, after a normalization error, config after a normalization error, ByteSize, integer range, UTF-8 in a Duration and in a config, a null, the budget) and TestLocatorManyFailuresLinear. The 60 s fuzz run found an edge case, a case-variant "speC" member: the config type must come from the decoded struct when the kind decode succeeds. Fixed; the input is kept as the corpus seed testdata/fuzz/FuzzChunkedDecode/0d47978f737fde90.

F4 and F13 (work units ignored bytes). Units now count bytes of strings, member names and number literals at every step that reads them: the UTF-8 check, scalar parse, number check, host lower-casing, appendJSON, locator number parses, materialize index keys, registry type, finder keys and texts, and get on equal-length keys. Each sort comparison (members, sets, keyed lists) and the duplicate scan charges 1 plus the common prefix. The Deprecations walk counts element text and segment-search bytes. Decode pieces now also split on decodeBytes (64 KiB): measure() counts text, and a member or element too large for any piece by bytes is decoded on its own. The work.go and package docs state the real bound: the longest single library call on one value. Tests: TestScaleBytes, TestYieldGapBytes (a counting clock is read at least once per decodeBytes; no call gets more than the budget plus one text), TestDecodePiecesBytes and TestDeprecationsCountedBytes.

F5 (nil nodes). One contract now: a nil node is JSON null everywhere. Guards added at each class member: normalize visit (reported as null), keyed nil entries and keys (no cascade into "no key member", for JSON null too), lowerHosts list and elements, registryDefaults spec, type and name, own's apiVersion, finder.at, appendJSON, measure, the locator, and Decode with a nil index. In convert: setAPIVersion, StripConversionData and the Deprecations apiVersion position. The schemaidx Select, ItemElem and Walk calls dereference a nil member value inside schemaidx, so I added workarounds in my packages: nullMembers in lookup.go and nullsFilled in convert. Tests: TestNilNodes (11 named cases through Resource and Run, with and without a lifecycle table), TestNilNodesEverywhere (every position of the example Bundle), TestNilNodeLookups and TestNullKeyNoCascade.

F7 (panic). Each Run worker recovers. The first panic stops dispatch, Run joins every worker, then raises a *resourcePanic in the caller; it wraps error values and carries the stack. A test-only `stopped` hook lets TestRunPanic pin the stop. TestRunPanic covers 1, 2 and 4 workers.

F8 (deprecations on canonical content). RZ-CFG-025 is skipped for tree.RoleCanonical resources. TestCanonicalNoDeprecations covers it.

F9 (charges without tests). TestStepCharges pins exact units for every charge, the six named ones included: chunker.size, foldCounts, finder.field index, the materialize presence index, pop and report. It also pins every new byte charge.

F10 (error returns of split pieces). TestChunkedDecodeErrors reaches the any-valued object and list, the typed list element, a struct member value, a map member name and the Duration UnmarshalJSON path. It also has a stage-level Plugin configSchema case.

F11 (piece boundary). Batches now count the object or array around them (pending starts at 1), and a member or element is large when 1+k > limit. TestChunkBoundary counts the nodes of each call from its actual JSON text (new work.decoded hook) and checks one size scan for a value of exactly limit nodes. It kills the k<limit mutant, the uncounted-wrapper mutant and the threshold mutants.

F12 (detector blind to -overlay). typeCheck honors an -overlay named in GOFLAGS (replaced, removed and added files), and go list inherits it. Proof: GOFLAGS=-overlay with the reviewer's M26 direct n.Get makes TestLookupsCounted fail, and so does an overlay-added file. The test doc states that a plain -overlay flag is not seen.

While checking for cascades I also removed a "tainted element" duplicate-skip I had added: RFC 8785 text keeps raw bytes, so strings that are not valid UTF-8 never falsely collide.

result.summary:
WP-39 round-2 findings (2 major, 9 minor) are all fixed at the root in internal/config/canonical. Before any code changed, each finding was reproduced on a snapshot of the sources (scratchpad wp39r4/orig), which was identical to the working tree, so no partial edits were on disk. Probes are in wp39r4/probe. Each fix was then proven by an overlay mutant that reverts it: wp39r4/mutants.py, 31 mutants, all killed, results in wp39r4/mutants.out.

**M1 option overflow.** Four members:
- (a) maxDiags+1 wrapping in newRun, newChecker and tooMany. countOption now clamps MaxDiagnostics, MaxResources and MaxValues to 2^30.
- (b) keeper.offer. The `2*k.n` test is now `len-n >= n`, and the sort count is pinned.
- (c) Encoder `workers*chunksPerWorker`. chunkCount no longer multiplies past n, and workerCount caps Workers at 256 for both encoder and decoder.
- (d) Decoder channel and goroutines. stream starts one goroutine per chunk it hands over, up to Workers-1, and the channel is bounded by 256.

Tests: TestDecodeOptionsClamped (caps {0, 1, MaxInt-1, MaxInt/2+1, MaxInt} x 5 finding kinds x workers {1, 3}), TestKeeperCost, TestChunkCount, TestEncodeWorkersClamped (1<<62, MaxInt*3/4, MaxInt), TestDecodeWorkersClamped (5000, 1<<40, 1<<50, MaxInt; same trees, bounded goroutines).

**M2 decode memory.** Members fixed:
- Chunk entries are allocated lazily.
- The parser no longer keeps resources elements (p.items and the resources node).
- Chunks drop their items and spans once checked.
- An element's entry is kept only while the decode can still succeed (run.fails). This also covers resources after the first one whose re-encoding differs (run.rejected).
- A chunk is not recorded once failure is known.
- A dropped element's tree is unlinked. Without this, the member and node slabs it shares with its neighbours kept every earlier Route alive: 48 MB held, now 224 KB.
- Document members other than resources, and a non-object document, are scanned, not built.
- New budgets DecoderOptions.MaxResources (DefaultMaxResources 20,000, the loader's) and MaxValues (DefaultMaxValues 2^26, one value per byte of the 64 MiB source). Past either, the decode returns one RZ-CFG-001 finding at the element or value that crosses it, and the parse stops there.
- The depth limit is moved into the same class: CodeLimit = RZ-CFG-001, previously RZ-CFG-027.
- ReadDump's scan now allows jsonval.MaxDepthLimit, so a dump whose content is too deep gets the decode's RZ-CFG-001 rather than ErrNotDump.

Measured:
- Live heap late in a failing 4 MiB decode is 166 to 224 KB beside the content, down from 5 to 48 MB.
- With raised limits, ReadDump allocates 50 to 75 bytes per body byte (was 140 to 150). With the default limits it is 3.3 to 5.9.
- A retained error keeps under 4 MiB of a 16 MiB content (was the whole content).

Tests: TestDecodeLimits, TestDecodeLimitPrecedence, TestDecodeRetention, TestDecodeFailingLiveHeap, TestDecodeAllocationPerByte, TestDecodeShallowValues. The owner decision on these limits is filed as a contract request.

**Minors:**
- **Lazy identity.** The ident struct builds the ResourceID and base path only on a resource's first finding, and shown decides without allocating (needsQuote). A clean decode now makes 0.15 (Routes) to 0.85 (ladder) allocations per resource, down from 4.2 to 4.9 (TestDecodeAllocsPerResource). BenchmarkVerify/5749 is 4,922 to 4,978 allocs/op (was 27,931 to 27,986) and 24 to 33 ms with 1 to 4 workers on this loaded 4-core host. ReadDump is 4,988 allocs/op and 34 to 39 ms.
- **Format of any non-string JSON type.** Number, float, object, array, null, bool and the empty string are now RZ-CFG-024 and stop the parse, as 02 req 33 says. doc.go and the test rows in TestDecodeNewer, TestDecodePrecedence and TestDecodeIdentity are updated.
- **Diagnostic text is a copy.** clip clones, which covers shown and boundElem keys, fields and string and number items. Class members tested in TestFindingsKeepNoContent: field name, resource identity, unknown kind, keyed key, document member, resource member, apiVersion member, re-encoding path, plus format as the control case.
- **encodeError path.** It now applies boundPath (TestEncodeErrorBounded covers Encode, EncodeResources, AppendNode and a root member, at depth 1 and 2).
- **Escaping.** An empty kind or name now shows as `""`; C1 controls, DEL, U+200B and U+2028 are quoted. The diag gap for path text is documented and filed as a contract request. TestIdentityEscapedPathsCarried checks the full line once diag escapes these characters.
- **Panic stop paths.** A new panic.go adds workPanic and capture. stream defers the channel close and wait, and check panics (inline or on a worker) are raised again on the caller after the join. parallel captures ctx.Err() and fn in both its inline and pooled paths. A checker's context error now goes to run.cancel, replacing chunk.err. Tests: TestDecodePanicSurfaces and TestEncodePanicSurfaces, with workers 1 and 4 and a goroutine-count baseline.
- **Docs.** The MaxDiagnostics and Findings comments now say that only newer findings stop the parse.
- **Mutants.** (a) TestNewerWalkCachesElem (white-box key cache plus an allocation slope for one set element). (b) The ReadDump depth rows in TestDecodeLimits. (c) TestAppendDumpDeep; this also found that dumpable accepted content at MaxDepthLimit whose dump no reader can read, so it now accepts up to MaxDepthLimit-1. (d) TestEnvelopeOrderKeys and a `{}` row in TestDecodeFormOrder.
- **Out-of-date API contract request.** Refiled below.

FuzzDecodeCanonical now also checks worker invariance under small limits and accepts RZ-CFG-001.

findings.issue:
Stage I copies the unbounded authored spec.slot into every per-Route and per-Upstream finding, and hashes it once per Route. The schema puts no maxLength and no pattern on PolicySpec.Slot (rendered.schema.json $defs/PolicySpec/properties/slot is a plain string), and the loader has no per-scalar limit below the 64 MiB source cap. As a result, the memory stage I uses for findings grows with the slot length times the finding count, not just the finding count. That breaks the Options.MaxDiagnostics promise ('bounded by the cap times the worker count, not by the input'), 02 req 78 (peak under 4x the canonical size) and the 01 req 54 / 02 req 78 time budgets. result.summary:
Adversarial review of WP-38 (internal/config/precedence/). Verdict: fix. I found one blocker and three minors; nothing else broke.

Blocker: stage I copies the authored spec.slot into every RZ-CFG-018 and RZ-CFG-019 message and hashes it once per Route. spec.slot has no length or pattern limit anywhere. A slot of 1 MiB shared by 1,000 Routes (about 2.1 MiB of input) leaves 1,006 MiB of findings on the heap. A 16 MiB slot on 10,000 Routes makes Run take 8.8 s with no findings at all. This breaks the documented findings-memory bound and 02 req 78. No filed contract request covers it.

Minors:
- Control characters in a slot can forge rows in the render --effective table.
- The removal sort in route() is not charged per comparison. The longest gap between yield-timer reads is 2.0 ms at 20,000 removals, against the 100 µs of 01 req 53. Unsized appends also leave uncharged gaps.
- A zero-value Resolver panics on Run and CheckPolicies, and the doc does not say to use New.

Probes that found nothing:
- Chaos run: 3,000 iterations under -race of random cancels, Body panics, workers 1 to 9 and yield clocks. No goroutine leaks or races. Every run returned results identical to the reference, ctx.Err() with no partial result, or a *unitPanic.
- Diagnostic cap: 3,000 random bundles with caps 1 to 8 and workers 1 to 7. Results always equal the sorted prefix of the uncapped list, and chains always match.
- Fuzz: FuzzPrecedenceInvariants ran 60 s, 600k execs, with no failures.
- Stress: three contended copies of the forEach, cancel and yield tests at -count=100 with -cpu=1,2,8 all passed.
- Checks: `go test -race -shuffle=on` passes with 99.9% coverage, and golangci-lint reports 0 issues.
- Code reading: no hostile-tree locator panic, no shared-slice aliasing, and no gap in the pool's stop/ctx ordering.

The probes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp38s2r1/. To rerun, use `go test -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp38s2r1/overlay.json -run TestProbe<Name> -v ./internal/config/precedence/` from /home/user/ruralz. findings.issue: The yield timer is not read while route() sorts its removed Gateway indexes. `removed := slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(fate))` walks a map and makes O(r log r) comparisons with no charge. Only afterwards does it charge r units, once (siteRemoved), so the timer is never read during the sort. This breaks 01 req 53 ('checked between units and every 256 nodes inside a unit'). It also falsifies the worker doc ('every loop whose length depends on the input counts its elements at its own site, so the time between two reads of the timer stays bounded') and the Resolve doc. TestWorkCharged pins siteRemoved at exactly n, so it cannot see this. Evidence: the probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/r38/mut/probe/probe_gap_test.go uses a real clock in Options.Now, YieldAfter 1h and GC off, and records the call site of each timer read. Command: `go test -count=1 -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/r38/mut/probe/ov_gap.json -run TestProbeYieldGap -v ./internal/config/precedence/`. Input: a Gateway of 19,000 ratelimit Policies (inside MaxResources 20,000) and one Route excluding all of them. Result: the longest stretch between two timer reads is 1.88 ms, about 19x the 100 µs target, from the read at route:438 (exclusion loop) to the read at route:475 (after the sort). Collect the keys of fate with one charge per key, then sort them with slices.SortFunc using a comparator that calls w.charge (siteRemovedSort or a new site), the way the stable sort by reason already does. Alternatively, append j in remove() and sort that slice with a charging comparator. Either way the timer is read every 256 comparisons. Add a TestWorkCharged row for this sort using the existing `sorting` bound. Add a yield test: one Route excluding n Gateway Policies, with a clock on which every read yields, asserting yields >= comparisons/256. It is also the local variable and parameter name for the Route's kept entries ([]attached) in route(), client() and cacheGuardrail(), where it shadows the type and makes the code harder to read.

The test actually asserts that merge(b, a) returns a's lower-rank entry first, which is the second list. The `<=` tie branch of merge is never exercised.

findings.issue: The test does not force two recorded panics: whether both units 1 and 2 panic depends on scheduling. The 'last panic wins' mutant (P6) is therefore killed only in about a third of runs; the engineer's own figure is 33 kills out of 100. The test passes reliably on correct code but proves the first-panic rule only by chance.
findings.fix: Make both panics deterministic with the existing hooks: unit 1 waits for unit 2's admitted event before panicking, and unit 2 waits for the stopped event before panicking. Add a test hook called under the gate after the failed decision so the test can order the two recoveries. Then assert that up.unit equals the stopped unit on every run.

findings.issue: mustNew(t, ...) runs inside a spawned goroutine. mustNew calls tb.Fatalf when New fails, and FailNow must run on the test goroutine. It is harmless today only because New cannot fail with these options.

Use a Yield callback that records how much of the bulk structure exists when it fires (for example a test hook counting inserts or bytes matched), and require at least one Yield before the loop ends for inputs of 1<<16 elements or 4 MiB. result.summary:
WP-36 round 1, adversarial lens: verdict fix, with one major and two minor findings.

The correctness core holds up:
- go test -race passes for both packages; CGO_ENABLED=0 with -shuffle=on passes; go vet is clean; golangci-lint reports 0 issues. Coverage is 99.5% (overlay) and 99.7% (subst).
- A 5-minute fuzz of FuzzOverlay and FuzzSubst (4 workers, run in a scratch copy of the repository) found nothing: 5.4M and 1.0M execs.
- Hand probes of the settle logic and the redispatch logic all behaved as specified: dispatch-member composites (removal-only lists, $patch-only objects, nested {$patch: replace}), ruralz.io/patch: replace with a removal-only type, type: null, a config list over a base map, and the reverse.
- Substitution keeps diagnostics free of values, except the header-name case in the second minor finding.

Major finding: both packages count work units correctly, but much of the work is charged in one call before or after a loop over the whole input, or not charged at all (schemaidx Select costs cases x members). The Yield calls then come in a burst after long stretches with no yield, which breaks 01 req 53.
- Overlay: an Upstream with 1M endpoints (22.8 MiB) runs 583 ms without a Yield.
- Subst: a 32 MiB scalar holding every detector needle runs 1.34 s without a Yield inside the detector regexps.
- PolicySpec with 1M members and type last: 307 ms (overlay) and 254 ms (subst) in one stretch, from the uncharged Select.

Minor findings:
- An overlay object with a duplicate key panics (merge.go:395) or silently overwrites a sibling member. The loader cannot reach this, but the precondition is not stated and the memberIndex comment suggests duplicates are handled.
- The credential header rule reads a header name substituted from a variable, and its message quotes that value. Both package docs say diagnostics never reveal a variable's value.

Probes and the overlay maps are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/w36adv1/probe/. No repository file was modified.

findings.issue:
The Yield contract the loader depends on (01 req 53: check every 256 nodes inside a unit, gosched once 100 µs have passed) holds by count but not in time. Each O(n) pass is charged in one charge() call, either before the pass or after it. So Yield fires n/256 times back to back, then not at all while the pass runs. A loader Yield that checks elapsed time yields once per burst and then runs for a long time without yielding.

Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp36ci1/probe/probe_gap_test.go, run with `go test -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp36ci1/probe/ov_gap.json -run TestProbeShapeYieldGap -v -count=1 ./internal/config/overlay/`. Results at n=400,000 entries (about 18 MB of source, within MaxSourceBytes), with the same figures under GOGC=off:

- 'map list entries deleted': longest gap 134-191 ms.
- 'orderedMap list merged and appended': 138-161 ms.
- 'labels merged, added and removed': 38-45 ms.
- 'redispatched Policy with a wide config': 37-44 ms.

A second probe, probe_yield_test.go via ov_yield.json, runs TestProbeSelectYieldGap on a Policy spec of 400k members with spec.type last and a composite overlay type, which makes settle run. The longest gap is 85 ms. That is twice the gap with type first, because each Select scans rules × members uncharged, and settle adds up to three Selects plus an uncharged Clone. TestYield only counts calls, so it cannot see any of this.

findings.issue:
The first undefined variable of a render builds the hint index over all HintNames inside one ApplyWith call, with no Yield. HintNames are the Environment's spec.variables keys, and the --environments file may hold 64 MiB.

Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp36ci1/probe/probe_hintidx_test.go, run with `go test -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp36ci1/probe/sv_hint.json -run TestProbeHintIndexUnmetered -v -count=1 ./internal/config/subst/`. The input is one Route whose spec.match.path.prefix is "${B}", with a Yield set:
- HintNames of 64 names × 512 KiB (32 MiB): Apply takes 502 ms and makes 0 Yield calls.
- 500,000 names × 64 bytes: Apply takes 784 ms with 0 Yield calls, and New takes another 107 ms sorting them, also without a Yield.

The scale shape 'req27 one long undefined name with near hints' at n=50,000 also shows a 191 ms gap (probe_sgap_test.go, sv_gap.json). Every other worker that reaches an undefined variable blocks in once.Do for the same time.
findings.fix: Meter the index build. Pass the caller's meter into index() and charge each name's length inside the build loop; with the once, the first caller pays and yields. Another option: build the index eagerly in New and document that New costs O(total HintNames bytes), so the loader calls it before stage E. Then add a TestHintCost row: a render whose only undefined variable meets 32 MiB of HintNames calls Yield at least (total bytes / byteUnit / yieldEvery) times during its first Apply. State New's sort cost in its doc.

result.summary:
WP-36 round 1 review, contracts and integration lens.

What holds:
- Both packages import only diag, schemaidx and tree plus the standard library, as section 1.2 allows.
- Every RZ code they use is registered: 001, 005, 006, 007, 008, 009, 010, 011, 013 and 030.
- Diagnostics have the shapes callers expect: Severity is always set, Resource, key-aware Path and Related are filled, and LimitDiagnostic carries no location.
- The MaxDiagnostics+1 contract matches diag.Collector's cap.
- Shared values are handled safely: CheckBase reads only, the Substituter's state is atomic or under a lock, regexps are safe for concurrent use, and Apply's output never aliases nodes, so substitution cannot visit a node twice.
- The new settle step and the RZ-CFG-006 redispatch are consistent with the rendered schema: dispatch is only kind at the root and spec.type in PolicySpec, each rule required plus const, with branches that only add config.
- Checks: build, vet, `go test -race -shuffle=on`, `CGO_ENABLED=0` tests and `bin/golangci-lint run` all pass (0 issues). Coverage is 99.5% for overlay and 99.7% for subst.

Two major findings, both about the Yield cadence the loader relies on for 01 req 53:
1. overlay charges each O(n) pass as one bulk unit. At 400k entries there are bursts of up to 7,811 Yield calls, followed by 130-190 ms with no call at all.
2. subst builds its hint index over every HintNames entry without any metering. With 30-32 MiB of names, one Apply runs 0.5-0.8 s with zero Yield calls.

Minor findings:
- 02 req 46 and test 19 conflict with how stage E handles $${ in CEL fields (and with the schemaidx NoSubstitution doc). A probe shows that a render following 02 req 46 reloads with RZ-CFG-011.
- The required order (CheckBase before Apply) is not stated anywhere. A probe shows a base $patch error is lost when the order is reversed.
- Section 3.1 lists too few codes for stage D.
- The round-3 contract request on the unresolved dispatch still says RZ-CFG-005; the code now reports RZ-CFG-006.

All probes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp36ci1/probe/ and run through go test -overlay. No repository file was changed.

findings.where: internal/config/overlay/fuzz_test.go:232-265 (dropRemovals and nullTree, the new FuzzOverlay metamorphic property wired at :186-202)
findings.issue:
The new property says that removing an overlay member whose value is a null tree, over a base scalar, changes neither the result nor the diagnostics. That is false, and the merge code is right in each case. The skips for $patch, the annotation and document positions only look at the member itself, never inside its value. nullTree counts a nested `$patch: null` member as a removal, and it lets through a value holding the ruralz.io/patch annotation key or a JSONSchemaDocument position at some depth. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp36s2r1q/probe/fuzz_test.go is the committed file with four seeds added. Run `go test -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp36s2r1q/probe/fz.json -run FuzzOverlay -count=1 ./internal/config/overlay/`. It fails seeds #46, #48, #50 and #52 with "a member holding nothing but removals over a base scalar changed the merge":
(1) base {"kind":"Route","spec":{"timeout":"5s"}}, overlay {"spec":{"timeout":{"$patch":null}}}. The merge reports RZ-CFG-005 "$patch is not valid in an object" (correct per 01 req 25). The pruned overlay reports nothing.
(2) The same with base Policy {"type":"cors","config":{}} and overlay {"spec":{"type":{"$patch":null}}}.
(3) base {"kind":"Route","metadata":{"annotations":"x"},...}, overlay {"metadata":{"annotations":{"ruralz.io/patch":null}}}. takeAction reports RZ-CFG-005 "unsupported ruralz.io/patch value null". The pruned overlay reports nothing.
(4) base Policy {"type":"validation.json-schema","config":"x"}, overlay {"spec":{"config":{"schema":{"k":null}}}}. config.schema is a JSONSchemaDocument, so {k:null} is data, and the merge correctly gives config {"schema":{"k":null}}. The pruned overlay keeps config "x".
A 2-minute fuzz run found none of these. Any fuzzing run that reaches these shapes will report a false failure, so the target cannot be relied on as it stands.
findings.fix: Make dropRemovals prune only values that really are nothing but removals. Reject a null tree holding a $patch key at any depth. Skip any member on the path to metadata.annotations["ruralz.io/patch"] whose value holds that key, not only the exact path. Reject a value when any position inside it is a JSONSchemaDocument: look up every nested path with documentAt on the base view, and on the merged view, or on the overlay root with the value in place. Add the four inputs above as FuzzOverlay seeds, each one failing against the current oracle. Then correct the FuzzOverlay doc and the dropRemovals doc to state the narrowed property.

findings.issue: No row of TestRedispatchRelated has an untested member whose composite replaces a base scalar ahead of the tested change in overlay order. It survives the suite (`go test -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp36s2r1q/mut/O10_blame_no_tested/ov.json ./internal/config/overlay/` prints ok). findings.issue: The doc says a member is named when the merge changed it by "removed, added, given another scalar or replaced by what remains of a composite". The code names an added member only when it is a scalar: a new composite goes to todo with base nil, so overScalar() is false. Probe TestProbeAddedComposite (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp36s2r1q/probe/probe_added_test.go, -overlay .../probe/added.json) uses nestedDispatch: base {"flag":true,"doc":{"$patch":1}}, overlay {"mode":{"k":1},"flag":false}. The related location is the overlay spec object (o.yaml:1:71), not the added mode member. The code is defensible, since a composite never satisfies a rule. The doc's two-way split ("changed" versus "left as the base wrote it") also leaves out the members that change but are never named: new composites and composites that replace composites. TestRedispatchRelated's own doc says it accurately: "a new or another scalar".
findings.fix: Reword dispatchPos and the blame comment to say what the code does. Example: "the first overlay member a dispatch rule tests whose scalar the merge changed: removed, a new or another scalar, or a scalar replaced by what remains of a composite; a composite never satisfies a rule, so a new composite, or one that merges into or replaces a base composite, is not named".

findings.issue: No TestScaleLinear shape takes the settle trial path, where composites replace base scalars and also change the dispatch, so every value is cloned and normalized once more. The linearity claim in the settle doc is untested. result.summary:
WP-36 round 1 review, lens tests and code quality. All the requested checks pass for internal/config/overlay and internal/config/subst: go build, go vet, `go test -race -count=1 -cover -shuffle=on -cpu 4` (coverage 99.5% overlay, 99.7% subst; repeated with -count=2 and shuffle, still stable), `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=1`, `bin/golangci-lint run` (0 issues), `bin/golangci-lint fmt --diff` (empty) and repocheck. I fuzzed FuzzOverlay for 120s and FuzzSubst for 90s in a scratch copy of the tree, with a private fuzz cache, and neither failed. I modified no repository file.

The settle fix is correct for every probe case (a) to (e) I re-derived. Of 19 merge.go mutants, 14 are killed, including: no budget check in settle, no trial, no Clone, no quiet flag, a nil schema in the trial, and the blame order and position rules. Of the survivors, O3 (always running the trial) is caught by the budget test, and O7, O14 and O20 are equivalent. Two survivors are real test gaps: O21 (settle before compactMembers, which panics on a simple input) and O10 (the tested() condition on blame). All five subst mutants on walker.literal and headerValue are killed, including S5, now killed by the new row and the new seeds. The comments and docs changed in subst (minors 3 to 7) match the code.

One major finding. The new FuzzOverlay metamorphic property (dropRemovals and nullTree) is false for values that hold a nested `$patch: null`, a nested ruralz.io/patch annotation key, or a JSONSchemaDocument position below the pruned member. Four one-line seeds make the property fail although the merge is correct, so fuzzing will report false failures. Minors: the two mutation gaps above, the dispatchPos doc saying \"added\" members are named while the code names added scalars only, and no linearity shape for the settle trial path (a probe shows a 4.00 ratio). Probes and mutants are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp36s2r1q/ (probe/, mut/, smut/).

findings.issue: checkExamples runs profile.Parse on every .yaml, .yml and .json file under examples/ and reports every parse finding. That includes files that are not Ruralz resources and files that a Bundle's .ruralzignore excludes, which 01 req 3 says are not part of the Bundle. Its doc says documents of other apiVersions are left out, but their parse failures are not. Probe (overlay test calling checkExamples on a temp tree): quickstart/compose.yaml containing `x-common: &common` and `<<: *common` gave three RZ-CFG-003 problems. shop-bundle/.ruralzignore `notes/` plus notes/draft.yaml gave `RZ-CFG-005 Route/draft: missing required field spec`. The CM shop-bundle itself passes: I extracted all 30 documents from the CM and none produced a problem.
findings.fix: Honor each Bundle root's .ruralzignore when walking (as 01 req 3 reads it). Either report parse findings only for files the loader would discover inside a Bundle root or control/, or record as the owner's decision that every YAML/JSON file under examples/ must parse under the restricted profile and say so in the doc comment. Add TestCheckExamples cases for a non-Ruralz YAML file with anchors and for an ignored file.

findings.issue: The RZ-CFG-006 message for $patch in a base document is `unknown field "$patch": $patch is allowed only in overlay files`. 01 req 25 quotes the text ("valid only in overlays"), and overlay.CheckBase (internal/config/overlay/merge.go:919) uses "$patch is valid only in overlays". So the same code, condition and position get different text depending on whether stage D or stage F reports it, for example through FromResources or any caller that skips CheckBase.
findings.fix: Word the stage F message as `unknown field "$patch": $patch is valid only in overlays` (or exactly the overlay text) and update TestErrorMapping case `req33 $patch in a base file`.

findings.issue: The doc comment says the test checks the position of each finding kind, including "the parent object of a missing field". Its input member `"retries": {}` produces no finding, though, and the expectation has only the enum and unknown-field lines. The required-at-parent position (01 req 33) is covered only by the golden required.diag.txt, not by this test as it claims.

findings.issue: schemaErrors is production code that only tests call (charge_test.go:131, numbers_test.go:858, scale_test.go:169). Pipeline code goes through check/runSchema, so this is a test helper living in the package API surface, and its doc comment duplicates runSchema's.

result.summary:
WP-35, spec-conformance lens: no blocker or major findings, five minors.

**Checks run, all passing:**
- Build and vet, including with `-tags integration`.
- `go test -race` and `CGO_ENABLED=0 -shuffle=on` (98.3% coverage).
- `golangci-lint` with and without the integration tag (0 issues); `golangci-lint fmt --diff` is empty; repocheck passes.
- The JSON-Schema-Test-Suite runs over 46 files and 1,301 cases with zero failures, and its number-bound variant passes too.
- `FuzzValidate` ran 60 s (about 1.96M execs) with no failure.
- Running `scripts/update-test-suites.sh json-schema` into a scratch `FIXTURES_ROOT` reproduced the pinned commit and SHA-256. `diff -r` against `test/fixtures/json-schema-test-suite` is empty.

**01 req 32:** met. The compiler uses draft 2020-12, formats and content as annotations, the refusing loader, and the seven-keyword vocabulary under `AssertVocabs`, parsed into Extensions. Tests cover each of these (TestRefusingLoader, TestFormatsNotAsserted, TestMetaVocabularyAssertsShapes, TestMetaVocabularyParsesKeywords) and fail when the setting is removed.

**01 req 33, probed through `-overlay` tests on the spec's stage F fixture cases:**
- RZ-CFG-006 is reported at the key, with nearest-name hints (`timout` hints `timeout`) and the dedicated `metadata.namespace` and top-level `status` messages.
- An unknown member of a closed config is RZ-CFG-006; an open config (`cors` `maxAge`) gives no finding.
- `rateLimit` hints `ratelimit`. A missing required field is reported at the parent object.
- The exactlyOneOf, atMostOneOf and atLeastOneOf messages name the fields.
- Duration and ByteSize failures use the CM syntax text.
- anyOf reports the branch that matches the instance's JSON type.
- RZ-CFG-012 covers PEM, `rediss://`, `secretRef: "abc"`, `{value: x}`, and literals in Policy configs (`auth.mtls`, `auth.upstream-oauth2`) and Upstream TLS fields. No value or authored member name is ever echoed.

**01 req 34:** duplicate keyed entries and set elements are RZ-CFG-005 at the second, with `related` pointing at the first. This holds for orderedMap and map lists, nested sets, and lists inside dispatched Policy configs.

**01 req 35:** the reserved-prefix check compares bytes exactly, reports at the key, and exempts only `ruralz.io/conversion-data`.

**11 req 18 and 19:**
- The JSON-Schema-Test-Suite is vendored with its LICENSE and SOURCE files and runs as an integration test in stage 8. Skipping every `optional/format` file is justified: the rendered and authoring schemas use no `format`.
- Both views compile, every `$ref` resolves, and all ten kinds and 23 Policy type dispatches exist.
- `examples/` does not exist yet. The CM shop-bundle, extracted from the docs, validates against the authoring view with zero problems.
- Loading each Bundle per Environment is forwarded to WP-75, whose scope already includes it.

**The five minors:**
- The meta-test harness reports parse findings for files that are not Ruralz resources and for files a Bundle's `.ruralzignore` excludes.
- The stage F `$patch` message wording differs from 01 req 25 and from `overlay.CheckBase`.
- TestPositions' comment claims it checks the required-at-parent position, but it doesn't.
- `schemaErrors` is production code that only tests call.
- One package-doc line is 122 columns long.

No repository file was modified; all probes lived under `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/rev/` and reached the package through `go test -overlay`.

findings.issue:
A zero literal of at most 64 bytes goes to jsonschema/v6 as written, whatever its exponent. Go's big.Rat.SetString parses the exponent with strconv.ParseInt before its zero special case, so for an exponent beyond int64 it returns (nil, false). The library then misbehaves:
- isInteger reports false;
- numValidate dereferences nil, which validate() recovers as errValidator;
- writeHash dereferences nil;
- equals reports false.

This breaks the package doc and the filed R-79 decision: "no literal ... makes it ... crash, and the diagnostics are those of the literal itself". A valid resource is rejected, and every other finding of the resource is replaced by one root diagnostic.

Reproduced through the YAML front end, the JSON front end and stage E substitution. Probes: probe1_test.go and probe2_test.go in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp35adv/, run with go test -overlay.

Exact inputs and what was observed:
- YAML Gateway with `telemetry: {traceSampling: 0e99999999999999999999}` (value 0, valid in [0,1]): `r.yaml:1:1 error RZ-CFG-005 Gateway/x: cannot be validated: the schema validator failed`. The literal 0 gives no diagnostic.
- The same through `${R}` with R=0e99999999999999999999 in Upstream circuitBreaker.failureRatio: same result.
- JSON listener `"port": 0e99999999999999999999`: `must be an integer, not a number`, where 0 gives `must be at least 1`.
- AIModel similarityThreshold: the real finding `spec: missing required field strategy` is lost.
- ByteSize: `must be an integer or quantity such as 10Mi`, where 0 gives nothing.
- IntOrString: a false type error.
- Numbers view: 15 of 18 fields differ from 0 for each of `0e99999999999999999999`, `-0e99999999999999999999`, `0e-99999999999999999999`, `0.0e9223372036854775808` and `0E` followed by 40 nines.

Why the tests miss it: the differential tests compare with rawValidate, which shares the library's mis-parse, and FuzzValidate's quickNumbers excludes exponents that do not fit.

findings.where: internal/config/schemaview/validate.go:379-380 (checkReserved), validate.go duplicateKeys (k.Kind after m.member), locate.go:214 memo.itemElem -> schemaidx.ItemElem/isKeyScalar (lookup.go:251), locate.go:199-204 memo.selectFor and Walk -> schemaidx cond.eval/constEqual (node.go:345,359)
findings.issue:
A member whose Value is nil crashes Validate with an unrecovered nil-pointer panic. Only the jsonschema call is behind recover, so the panic reaches the loader worker, and a ruralzd reload does not survive it.

The package already treats nil member values as legal input: work.instance converts them to null, TestInstance has a "nil member value" case, and varsBelow, walkUnits and knownPos guard nil. Stage G also documents that "FromResources trees may hold" nil nodes, and FromResources runs stage F (01 req 52).

Probes probe3_test.go and probe4_test.go, run with go test -overlay:
- Gateway with metadata `"labels"` set to Value nil: `panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` at validate.go:380 (`pairs.Kind`; m.member returns (nil, true)).
- Gateway listener entry with `"name"` set to Value nil: panic in schemaidx.isKeyScalar (lookup.go:251), from schemaidx.ItemElem, from memo.itemElem (locate.go:214), from memo.step.
- Policy with spec `"type"` set to Value nil: panic in schemaidx.constEqual (node.go:359), from cond.eval and Node.Select, through memo.selectFor and Walk.
- duplicateKeys has the same defect in code: `k, ok := m.member(item, key); if !ok || (k.Kind != ...` dereferences a nil k.
findings.fix:
Treat a nil node as JSON null everywhere in the mapping.
- checkReserved: skip or treat as non-map when pairs == nil.
- duplicateKeys: skip when k == nil.
- Audit every m.member and memo.get caller for this class.
- schemaidx nil safety for ItemElem (isKeyScalar) and cond.eval (constEqual): file a contract request with WP-03, or guard inside schemaview by passing a shared KindNull node wherever a member Value is nil.
- Optionally add a recover around the mapping in ValidateWith that reports the same RZ-CFG-005 "cannot be validated" finding, so a mapping defect never stops the process.

Add one table case per member: labels nil, annotations nil, keyed key nil, dispatch member nil, set and list items nil, and a nil value under a shadowed duplicate. Each must fail on the current code.

findings.where: internal/config/schemaview/validate.go runSchema (the validate() call), locate.go:199-204 memo.selectFor and checkLists Walk dispatch; work.go:62-84 (Options.Yield doc); 01 req 53
findings.issue:
01 req 53 requires a yield check every 256 nodes inside a unit, with a 100 µs target (architecture OQ-performance-budgets-and-benchmarking-6 (a)). Stage F charges two spans only after they finish, and both grow with the whole resource: the jsonschema/v6 Validate call and the schemaidx Select dispatch. Select costs about 23 cases times a linear inst.Get per object.

JSON documents have no MaxDocumentTokens cap (01 req 6 caps YAML documents only), so one resource can reach 64 MiB. The exception is recorded only in the Options.Yield Go doc. I found no OQ row, R row or contract request for it.

Probes probe5_test.go, probe6_test.go and probe9_test.go, run with go test -overlay and wall clock:
- Valid Gateway, 200,000 listeners (10,488,994 bytes, 800,007 nodes): the single validate() span takes 464 ms with no Yield call inside.
- The same Gateway with a type error in each port: 410 ms span; whole-call maximum gap 448 ms.
- largeRoute(1,000,000): maximum gap 178 ms.
- largePolicy(300,000): maximum gap 367 ms.
- largePolicy(1,000,000): one memo.selectFor span of 92 ms, charged 1,000,002 units only after it; checkLists maximum gap 90 ms.
- 1,000,000 valid allowOrigins: maximum gap 208 ms.
findings.fix:
Choose one:
- Bound the spans. Validate large keyed lists and sets element by element with the compiled item definition, yielding between elements, and validate the container's own keywords separately. File a contract request with schemaidx for a dispatch that indexes the object's members once, so one Select reads O(cases) members.
- Or file a contract request that records the exception where the next reader looks: an 01 req 53 amendment or OQ row stating that stage F yields only between validator and dispatch spans, the bound on a span (for example a node cap per JSON document, as MaxDocumentTokens does for YAML), and the measured cost.

Either way, add a deterministic test that counts the nodes processed inside the longest uncharged span against a stated budget.

findings.where: internal/config/schemaview/schemaview.go:19-20 (package doc), validate.go:31-34 (Validate doc), validate.go duplicateKeys and duplicateElements messages
findings.issue:
The package and Validate docs say a finding about a substituted value "names them, never their values". The duplicate messages quote the substituted value.

Probe probe10_test.go (afterSubstitution):
- `trustedProxies: ["${DB_PASSWORD}", "${DB_PASSWORD}"]` with DB_PASSWORD=hunter2-s3cr3t gives `duplicate element "hunter2-s3cr3t" in a set; variable "DB_PASSWORD" was substituted into the element; ...`.
- Two listeners with `name: ${L}` give `duplicate entry: name "hunter2-s3cr3t" is already used by an earlier entry; ...`.

The paths (`[item=hunter2-s3cr3t]`, `[name=hunter2-s3cr3t]`) carry the value as 01 req 48 requires, so the doc's guarantee does not hold either way.
findings.fix:
Choose one:
- When k.Vars or varsBelow is non-empty, word the duplicate messages without the value (the path already locates the element) and add a test that the value is absent from the message.
- Or correct both docs to say only that the variables are named, and that keyed and set path elements show the values as 01 req 48 requires.

findings.issue: Secret findings are grouped by path text alone (map[*textNode]*secretFinding). Two different x-ruralz-secret positions that render the same path text, such as the secretRef of two keyed entries that share a key, are merged into one RZ-CFG-012 at the first position. The second value then either gets no RZ-CFG-012 at its own location, or its reasons are attributed to the first entry. Probe through go test -overlay with envelope("Consumer", `{"credentials": {"apiKeys": [{"name": "k", "secretRef": {"provider": "env", "name": "A", "x": 1}}, {"name": "k", "secretRef": "LITERAL"}]}}`): one RZ-CFG-012 at r.json:1:146 reading "invalid secret reference: the field accepts only key, name or provider; the field must be an object; ...". The 'must be an object' reason belongs to the second entry, which gets no RZ-CFG-012. With the entry order reversed, the second entry's unknown member is dropped completely: only 'a literal value is not allowed' is reported, at 1:146. The resource still fails, because a duplicate-key RZ-CFG-005 is also reported, but 01 req 33 requires an RZ-CFG-012 for each non-conforming secret value, and 01 req 51 requires every error to surface in one run.
findings.fix: Group secret findings by position, not by path text: key m.secrets by the secret position's node pointer (p.secret.node), or by (textNode, pos). Add a table test for both entry orders. Each test asserts one RZ-CFG-012 per entry, at that entry's location, carrying only that entry's reasons.

findings.issue: The package doc and the View.Validate doc both say that a finding about a value stage E substituted into 'names the variables, never their values (01 req 29)'. That is false for duplicate keys and duplicate set elements. Probe: set Vars ["SECRETISH"] on two set elements "VALUE-FROM-ENV" in spec.match.hosts, or on two listener names. The output is `spec.match.hosts[item=VALUE-FROM-ENV]: duplicate element "VALUE-FROM-ENV" in a set; variable "SECRETISH" was substituted into the element...`, and the same pattern for `duplicate entry: name "VALUE-FROM-ENV"`. The substituted value appears in both the message and the path. 01 req 29 only requires naming the variable, and 01 req 48 requires the value in the path, so the behavior is allowed. The doc is what is wrong.
findings.fix: Reword both docs. The substituted clause names variables and never their values; a duplicate key or set element is quoted as its path shows it. Alternatively, drop the quoted value from the duplicate messages, since the path already carries it. Add a test that pins whichever choice is made.

findings.issue: Compile's doc says that idx 'must have been loaded from the same bytes' and that Compile checks the root kind dispatch against it. Only the set of kinds is checked. Probe: Compile on the rendered bytes with every "const": "ruralz/v1alpha1" replaced by "ruralz/v1alpha2", paired with the v1alpha1 index, returns nil error. View.APIVersion() then reports ruralz/v1alpha1, but the view rejects every v1alpha1 resource ('apiVersion: must be "ruralz/v1alpha2"'), and NewSet files it under the wrong version. The 01 test plan row 030 (a test-only second view in schemaview.Set) is exactly the case that can pair them wrongly. The package's own meta test (authoringView) also breaks the stated precondition: it pairs authoring bytes with the rendered index.
findings.fix: In Compile, require the root apiVersion const of the document to equal idx.APIVersion(), and refuse otherwise with ErrSchema. Reword the precondition to what is actually supported: an index of a view of the same apiVersion with the same kinds, which is how the authoring meta test uses it. Add a TestCompileErrors row for a mismatched apiVersion.

findings.issue: The exported default cap is named MaxDiagnostics. The six sibling stages that WP-69's pipeline wires next to it all export DefaultMaxDiagnostics: overlay, profile, subst, defaults, precedence and canonical. In schemaview the name also duplicates the field name Options.MaxDiagnostics, so the facade gets one stage with a different API spelling.
findings.fix: Rename the constant to DefaultMaxDiagnostics, as overlay.DefaultMaxDiagnostics is named, and update the docs and tests that reference it.

findings.issue: The Options.Yield doc does not say which goroutine calls the hook, or whether one function shared by ValidateWith calls on several workers must be safe for concurrent use. overlay.Options.Yield and subst.Options.Yield both state this rule, and WP-69 passes one Yield per worker to every stage.
findings.fix: Add the same sentence the siblings use: ValidateWith calls Yield only on its calling goroutine, so a per-worker function needs no lock, and one shared across concurrent calls must be safe for concurrent use.

findings.issue: For the 01 req 25 rule '$patch in a base document: RZ-CFG-006', stage F's message is `unknown field "$patch": $patch is allowed only in overlay files`. overlay.CheckBase reports the same rule with the same code as "$patch is valid only in overlays" (internal/config/overlay/merge.go:919), which matches the spec text ('valid only in overlays'). One rule therefore has two wordings, depending on which stage caught it. In practice stage F's wording is reachable only where CheckBase has not run, such as FromResources.
findings.fix: Use the spec's and overlay's wording, `unknown field "$patch": $patch is valid only in overlays`, and update mapping_test.go:73.

result.summary:
Verdict: pass, with six minor findings and no blocker or major. Lens: contracts and integration.

Every check I ran passes:
- go test with -race -shuffle=on (46 s), and again with CGO_ENABLED=0.
- The JSON-Schema-Test-Suite runner under the integration tag (11 req 18).
- go vet; bin/golangci-lint run ./internal/config/schemaview/... (0 issues); repocheck.
- The schemaview tests in defaults and overlay that call this package.
- Benchmarks: 18.6 ms per compile, about 57 µs per valid Gateway.

Contracts and integration:
- The package imports only what 1.2 and 1.3 allow: schemaidx, diag, tree, api/schema and jsonschema/v6. No jsonschema type appears in its exported API.
- It follows the committed contracts it uses. Diagnostics have the diag.Diagnostic shape with Resource, key-aware Path, Location and Related. Paths come from schemaidx.ItemElem. Walk uses ErrSkipChildren. The codes RZ-CFG-005, 006 and 012 are registered.
- The exported API covers what WP-69 and the CLI need: Embedded(schemaidx.Set), NewSet, Set.View, Set.Served, and Set.ValidateWith(res, files, Options{MaxDiagnostics, Yield}).
- The cap+1 behavior matches the sibling stages and diag.Collector.
- Duplicate members resolve first-wins, as tree.Get and schemaidx dispatch do.
- Results come back in diag.List.Sort order; a probe compared the returned order with a re-sorted copy.
- Views and Sets are immutable and the tree is never mutated. TestConcurrentValidate passes under the race detector.
- No secret value reached any message in my probes.
- Keyed-entry identity agrees with overlay's entryID. Stage F is stricter in one way: it treats 1 and 1.0 as the same key.

The minor findings, each confirmed by a probe under go test -overlay (probes kept in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp35c):
1. Secret findings are grouped by path text alone. For two keyed entries with the same key, the RZ-CFG-012 findings are merged or misattributed to the first entry.
2. The docs say substituted values never appear in findings, but duplicate key and duplicate element messages quote them.
3. Compile does not check that the document's apiVersion matches the index's.
4. The default cap is named MaxDiagnostics, while the six sibling stages use DefaultMaxDiagnostics.
5. The Options.Yield doc does not say whether a hook shared across goroutines must be safe for concurrent use.
6. The `$patch` message is worded differently from overlay's message for the same rule.

TestMetaExamples is skipped until examples/ exists (WP-53). Loading each Bundle under examples/ through the pipeline is left to WP-75, whose scope includes it.

findings.issue: This test fails in the Go 1.26 floor job, which runs `make floor` (pr-fast job 4: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8 GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -shuffle=on ./...). Command: `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8 GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=1 -shuffle=on ./internal/config/schemaview/`. Output: `--- FAIL: TestLongTextAlloc/quoted_unknown_name ... mapping allocated 25221720 bytes for a 4194464-byte document (6.0 per byte), want at most 6.0 per byte` (6.01). It failed the same way in 3 of 3 runs and is the only failing test on the floor. A memory profile (-memprofilerate=1) shows where the bytes go: about 20 MB of the 24.6 MB is diag.Path.String quoting the 4 MiB field name. It calls diag.marshal, then json.Encoder.Encode, then encoding/json/v2 MarshalWrite, and the bytes.Buffer grows from empty. Under the 1.26 jsonv2 experiment that allocates about twice what Go 1.27.1 does (3.0 per byte there). The test comment says the budgets hold with and without -race and lists figures for 1.27 only. The budget's margin was never checked on the floor toolchain, so the 6.0 limit sits right at the measured value.
findings.fix: Measure every allocation-budget case on go1.26.8 with GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 as well as go1.27.1 with and without -race. The class is the four TestLongTextAlloc cases, TestQuoteBoundedAlloc and TestLargePathElements; the other cases passed on the floor at 1.00, 2.01 and 2.01 against limits of 2, 4 and 4. Set the quoted-name budget with a margin shown on all of them (for example 8 per byte) and record the floor figures in the comment. Also file a contract request against WP-01 diag: rendering a quoted path segment should pre-size its buffer, or quote without growing a json.Encoder buffer from empty. That growth is the root cause of the 6x allocation, and it lies outside this package.

findings.where: internal/config/schemaview/mapping.go:207-220 (mapper.record prune trigger and bound check); tests: cap_test.go, work_test.go:736 TestYieldPrune
findings.issue: No test notices if pruning or the early-drop bound is removed, so the documented invariant 'out holds fewer than 2*keep diagnostics ... so memory stays bounded' is untested. Three mutants pass the whole suite (`CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=1 -overlay <mutant>/overlay.json ./internal/config/schemaview/` gives ok in about 10 s for each): (1) never prune, the condition replaced by `if len(m.out) < 0 {`; (2) prune at 4*keep, `if len(m.out)/4 >= m.keep {`; (3) no bound early-drop, `if false {` in place of `m.bound != nil && m.compareEntries(&e, m.bound) >= 0`. The never-prune mutant matters in practice. For a Gateway listener with 200,000 integer hostnames (200,000 type errors) at a cap of 10, m.out holds 200,000 entries instead of 11. The live heap after mapErrors (measured with runtime.GC and HeapAlloc) doubles from 70 MB to 141 MB. TestYieldPrune calls m.prune() directly, so it cannot see that record never calls it. TestTruncationDeterministic and TestMaxDiagnosticsOption compare only the returned list, which is the same without pruning. The same applies to the scale tests' allocation and scan budgets, which still hold without the bound comparison that TestLongSiblingPrefixes' ascending cases describe exercising.
findings.fix: Add a table test that records many distinct entries under small caps (keep 2, 3 and 8; 10*keep entries in ascending, descending and permuted order). After every record it should assert len(m.out) < 2*m.keep, that m.bound is non-nil once 2*keep entries have been seen, and that recording an entry that sorts at or after m.bound leaves len(m.out) and m.seen unchanged. In TestLargePathElements or TestLongSiblingPrefixes, assert len(m.out) <= 2*m.keep after mapErrors. Each mutant above, never-prune, prune at 4*keep and no bound, must then fail; show this with -overlay.

result.summary:
WP-35 round-3 review (lens: tests and code quality). The scoped checks pass on Go 1.27.1: go build, go vet, go test -race -cover -shuffle=on (98.3% coverage, 192 s), CGO_ENABLED=0 go test, bin/golangci-lint run (0 issues), bin/golangci-lint fmt --diff (clean) and go run ./internal/tool/repocheck. Blocker: the Go 1.26 floor job fails. With GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8 GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 CGO_ENABLED=0, TestLongTextAlloc/quoted_unknown_name allocates 6.01 bytes per document byte against a budget of 6.0, in 3 of 3 runs. Mutation testing used 39 mutants of the round-3 code, run through -overlay. 35 were killed, among them first-wins in the instance, the shadowed skips, the repeated-reserved-key check, the lcp peer cache and memo, clip, every new charge site, step.find's compare count, the keep clamp and the prune overflow. findings.issue:
02 req 54 says that in M1 the identity conversion must still run the full rewrite-and-compare path. The convert package documents this: "Converting to the same apiVersion still runs both halves, so render --api-version exercises the whole path in M1 (02 req 54)". No test fails when Convert skips either half for the same version.

Repro 1, skip both halves: an overlay copy of convert.go adds `if from == to && r.Serves(from) { return doc, nil }` before the ToHub call (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/rv37s/mut/convert.go, overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/rv37s/mut/overlay.json). Repro 2, skip only FromHub: `if from == to { return hub, ds }` before the FromHub call also survives.

The effect is observable. Run Default().Convert("ruralz/v1alpha1", "ruralz/v1alpha1", "Route", doc, false) on doc = {"apiVersion":"ruralz/v1alpha1","kind":"Route","metadata":{"name":"a","annotations":{"ruralz.io/conversion-data":"x"}},"spec":{}}. findings.where: internal/config/defaults/normalize.go:263 (normalizer.visit); internal/config/defaults/gate_test.go:155 (TestCanonicalNumberGrammar is the only canonical-role gate case)
findings.issue:
The package docs (defaults.go step 3, the Normalize doc) and the round-4 report say Normalize is the gate for what the canonical form cannot hold "in every tree, canonical content included". findings.issue: memberSchema descends into typed-map values through sel.Values(). The package doc says defaults are materialized "in list entries, typed-map values and a Policy config", and normalization and the decode use the same helper. No test reaches a typed-map value schema.
