Confirmed. Part (a) is a real code defect in the owned file internal/config/canonical/decode.go. array() at about line 1085 and object() at about line 1130 copy the finished container out of the scratch stacks and truncate them with p.items[:base] and p.members[:base], but never clear the tail. The backing arrays keep a pointer to every leaf node of the last wide list or object. unlink() in stream.go clears the member and item links of a dropped element, but not these scratch pointers, so every 512-node slab those leaves sit in stays reachable for the rest of the parse.

This contradicts three statements:
- doc.go 134-139: a failing decode "keeps no element it has checked" and "holds about twice the content".
- The checker.run comment in stream.go: "a failing decode holds no more than the elements in flight".
- The ~1 MiB bound that TestDecodeFailingLiveHeap claims to guard.

Clearing the tails removes the retention: 57.3x falls to 4.2x and 16.2x to 6.9x. A wide list and a wide object stay retained together: 331 MB held for 14.7 MB of content, about the sum of the two. What remains after the fix is scratch capacity (about 9 MB of item pointers and about 87 MB of members), so fix step 2, releasing oversized scratch at element boundaries, is also needed before the doc's figure can be true.

The newerWalk.frames member of the class is real but smaller than "keeps the slabs of the last walked resource alive" might suggest. unlink() has already cleared the links of the dropped element, so each stale frame.item keeps only its own slab of about 57 KB, at most schema-depth of them. My probe could not measure it apart from noise (80 B). It still belongs in the class fix: clear the frames in start, or nil frame.item on pop.

Part (b) reproduces as stated. A decode already known to fail still builds the element in flight in full, at about 65x its bytes. The design arguably needs that tree, because the newer walk must still find the newer findings inside that element, and the doc does mention "the elements in flight" and the 8 GiB figure for a one-resource dump. So (b) is a documentation error plus a test gap rather than a code defect: "a failing decode of hostile content holds about twice the content" is false whenever an element is wide. The absolute peak stays bounded by MaxValues in every case.

Severity is major rather than minor because:
- The package's documented memory bound for hostile input (the ReadDump path) is wrong by more than an order of magnitude because of a code defect.
- Its regression test misses the shape.
- The stale retention can roughly double the in-flight peak, since the list and object stacks add up.
- All fixes lie inside the owned directory: the clear() calls and frames reset, releasing oversized scratch, the doc.go and MaxValues doc corrections, and wide-element test rows proved by overlay. result.note:
Confirmed. The current stream.go keeps both documented bounds. One is "runs on at most Workers goroutines" (doc.go:184-188, DecoderOptions.Workers in decode.go:75-81, the stream comment). The other is "a channel that holds at most Workers-1 chunks". The baseline probes stay exactly at those bounds.

No test pins either bound reliably:
- TestDecodeWorkersClamped tests only huge worker counts, so the chunk count is the only limit it checks (extra <= n/streamChunk). Mutant A goes back to starting one goroutine for every chunk handed over, which falls in the class of the earlier WP-39 finding ("Workers 5,000 started 4,999 goroutines"). The suite does not catch it: with Workers 2 or 3, 61 to 87 goroutines run instead of 1 or 2.
- TestDecodeFailingLiveHeap runs with Workers: 1 only.
- TestDecodeCapStopsParse catches mutant B only some of the time, depending on scheduling (about 2 of 4 full-suite runs, 1 of 5 isolated runs, 0 of 1 under -race).

The finding is slightly overstated on one point: it says B "passes the whole suite", but B is caught some of the time. That still is not a test that fails without the fix, which is what the AGENTS.md quality standard requires ("Prove it by ... a mutation the test kills"; deterministic tests). With B, a failing decode whose workers are stalled holds every chunk in flight: 93 of 93 in the probe, against a bound of 4. That breaks the memory bound the round-2 M2 fix depends on, and no test runs that fix with Workers above 1.

I rate this major, not minor. The code is correct today, but the stated concurrency and memory guarantees of an exported API, and the regression test for an earlier finding, can be broken without any deterministic test noticing.

Suggested fix:
- Count goroutines started and the most chunks queued or in check at once, with an internal counter or test hook in stream or run. A peak sampled with NumGoroutine depends on scheduling.
- Stall the workers so the channel fills for certain. Gating ctx.Err on worker goroutines, as the probe does, works.
- Assert started <= W-1 and handed-over chunks <= 2*(W-1) for Workers 2, 3 and 8.
- Add Workers 3 rows to TestDecodeFailingLiveHeap.
- Show that both mutants are killed.

result.summary:
I found one major and four minor findings in WP-38 round 2 (adversarial lens). The verdict is fix.

**Major: the diagnostic cap does not hold with more than one worker.** Each worker keeps up to MaxDiagnostics+1 findings for the whole call, and admits() only checks that worker's own heap. So the findings held and built grow with the worker count. On the round-3 blocker's shape (1,000 Policies x 400 Routes, 400,000 RZ-CFG-020 findings), the live heap was 6 MiB at 1 worker, 74 MiB at 16, 109 MiB at 64 and 257 MiB at 400 workers. Run's TotalAlloc went from 50 MiB to 1,133 MiB. From about 8 workers up this exceeds the 02 req 78 memory target. Stage G avoids this with a per-unit buffer and one shared keeper.

**Minor findings:**
- **Goexit in an injected callback:** a Body (or Now) that calls runtime.Goexit makes the pooled path return success while silently dropping the Policy. In the probe an authz.cel Policy vanished from the chain and the RZ-CFG-038 finding with it; stage G treats this case as an error.
- **Memory for absent references:** stage I spends about 309 bytes per reference to a Policy that does not exist, all for references it skips. That is 63 MiB on 4.6 MB of YAML, and about 1.2 GB at the 64 MiB source limit.
- **Zero-Phase replacement:** an empty headers or transform Policy still replaces a Gateway Policy in its slot but gets no row in render --effective. The specs do not say what should happen, so this needs an owner decision.
- **Bulk charges:** three sites charge their work only after a full pass, contrary to the work.go doc. The resource limit keeps each pass to about 20,000 elements.

**The round-1 slot fix holds:** I found no regression in slot clipping or interning.

**Checks I ran:**
- `go test -race -shuffle=on` on the package passes.
- The concurrency, yield and cap tests pass 40 times each at -cpu=1,2,4,8 under the race detector.
- FuzzPrecedenceInvariants ran 120 s (380k execs) in a copy of the repository outside the working tree, with no failure.
- Wall-clock gaps between timer reads were dominated by allocation and GC and by other load on the machine. They support no finding, so I report the bulk-charge minor from the code alone.

All probes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp38-advr2-q4z/ (files probe_cap_test.go, probe_goexit_test.go, probe_absent_test.go, probe_zero_test.go, probe_gap_test.go and probe_gap2_test.go, each with its overlay_*.json). They run through `go test -overlay` against /home/user/ruralz/internal/config/precedence/. I did not modify any repository file.

The code limits them correctly, with p.path.isField("metadata") and p.path == nil, but no test covers an unknown `namespace` or `status` field anywhere else. With the status mutant, the input envelope("Upstream", `{"protocol": "http", "endpoints": [{"address": "a:1", "status": 1}], "status": {}}`) reports `spec.status: unknown field "status": only Ruralz Control writes status` and `spec.endpoints[address=a:1].status: ... only Ruralz Control writes status`. result.summary:
WP-35 round-2 review, spec conformance lens. No blocker or major findings; two minor test gaps.

Checked against 01 H 32-35, 11 B 18-19, the 4.4 Done-when line and the design-document sections they cite:
- 01 req 32: draft 2020-12, formats as annotations only, a loader that refuses every URL, and the vocabulary asserted on every schema and parsed into Extensions. Tests cover each of these.
- 01 req 33: I probed every stage-F row of the 01 test plan for RZ-CFG-005, 006 and 012 through go test -overlay. Every code, path, position, message and hint matched the spec:
  - required findings sit at the parent and name the field;
  - unknown fields are reported at their key with the nearest name as hint, with the special wording for metadata.namespace, top-level status and $patch;
  - enum hints work (rateLimit suggests ratelimit);
  - the combination keywords name their fields;
  - the anyOf branch matching the instance's JSON type is the one reported;
  - Duration and ByteSize failures use the documented syntax text;
  - RZ-CFG-012 never contains the value or an authored member name.
- 01 req 34: duplicates are reported at the second entry with the first as related location.
- 01 req 35: the reserved ruralz.io/ prefix and the conversion-data exemption both compare exactly.
- 11 req 18: TestJSONSchemaTestSuite ran 46 files and 1,301 cases with zero failures. I fetched commit 5b0ee16: the SHA-256 of its `git archive` tar matches SOURCE, the vendored tests/draft2020-12, remotes and LICENSE are byte-identical to it, and scripts/update-test-suites.sh run into a scratch directory reproduces test/fixtures/json-schema-test-suite exactly. The empty format list is justified, since neither schema file uses `format`.
- 11 req 19: both schema files compile, every $ref resolves, all 10 kinds and 23 Policy types dispatch, and the vocabulary agrees with schemaidx. TestMetaExamples skips for now because examples/ does not exist yet (WP-53 adds it). Loading each Bundle through the pipeline is forwarded to WP-75, whose scope covers it.
- Every error kind maps to a registered code (005, 006 or 012).

Checks run, all green: race tests (80 s), CGO_ENABLED=0, the Go 1.26.8 floor with GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2, the integration tag, golangci-lint run and fmt (also with the integration tag), repocheck, and a 60-second FuzzValidate run. Statement coverage is 98.4%.

The two minor findings are test gaps, not wrong behavior:
1. Nothing tests that the namespace and status wordings stay at metadata.namespace and the top level. Mutants that apply them at any depth survive the whole suite.
2. Three branches of the RZ-CFG-012 reason builder are never run: wrapper kinds without causes, type errors without a schema type, and the default case. A mutant that puts the value into the default reason survives, so nothing tests that the value is kept out of those reasons.

All probes and mutants used overlays in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/r2/; no repository file was modified.

findings.where: internal/config/precedence/work.go:40-47 (claim); resolve.go:222-231 addKeys, :302-303 and :314 selectOne b.Get, :357 attachList sels lookup, :474 exclusion byName lookup, :752-778 legOrder; locate.go:143 and :148-156 listLoc.entry
findings.issue: The round-1 fix charges slot text by bytes (siteSlotIntern, 1+len/byteUnit) but not the other authored text of unbounded length that stage I hashes and compares: reference names. The schema gives PolicyRef.name, RouteUpstream.name and CompositionStep.upstream no maxLength. Stage I still runs when references do not resolve (02 req 40). Each such name costs one work unit however long it is, so the documented promise breaks: work.go says 'the time between two reads of the timer stays bounded', and Options.Now says 'stage I shares the processor with live traffic during activation'. Exact input: one Route whose spec.policies holds 4 unresolved names of 12 MiB each (48 MiB, inside the 64 MiB source cap). The same holds for spec.upstreams with 4 such names, and for spec.excludePolicies with 4 such names against a Gateway of 16 Policies. Command: go test -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp38-r2tq-k8m/ov_gap.json -count=1 -run TestProbeRefGap -v ./internal/config/precedence/ (probe: .../wp38-r2tq-k8m/probe/probe_refgap_test.go). Observed with YieldAfter 100 µs, over 4 runs, longest gap between two Options.Now reads: 13-21 ms for policies (24 clock reads in the whole Run), 9-20 ms for upstreams (6 reads), 6.5 ms for exclusions (36 reads). The short-name baseline is 7-135 µs. Class members, each an uncharged O(len) hash or compare per occurrence: addKeys inserting into s.sels (Gateway, Route and Upstream lists); selectOne s.b.Get for the Policy and for the Plugin reference; the attachList sels lookup; the route() exclusion lookup in gateway.byName; the listLoc.entry name compare and its byName index; legOrder's sort comparisons, seen map and s.upstreams lookup for spec.upstreams and composition steps. Not covered by the round-1 deviation (which covers slots only, with a slot-length contract request), and the report files no contract request for reference lengths.
findings.fix: Stage F bounds every metadata.name to 63 bytes, so a longer reference can never resolve. At every member site, treat a reference name longer than 63 bytes as unresolved (skip it as sel==nil or missing) before any map operation or comparison. Add one TestWorkCharged/TestSlotWorkOnce-style row per site, asserting that work units and clock reads do not grow with a reference's length above 63 bytes. Under the mutant, b gets a's slice and still runs p02 and p03; the original passes (.../ov_memo.json). genBundle draws at most 6 Gateway entries, so positions are single digits and the model-based fuzz target cannot reach a collision.

Assert each Route's onRequestHeaders names and that the two slices are not shared (sameArray false), and prove it with the A44 overlay. Optionally let genBundle sometimes draw a Gateway list of 11 or more entries, so the model comparison sees multi-digit positions.

It fails under the mutant with 'onRequestHeaders: cap 3, len 2' and 'onResponse: cap 2, len 1', and passes on the original (.../ov_cap.json).
findings.fix: Add a same-Phase replacement Route, such as one listing a cors Policy that replaces cors-g, to TestClientPhaseSharing so its cap==len loop covers it. Or assert cap==len in TestReplaceAndExclude. Prove it with the A51 overlay.

findings.issue: The doc says clip 'allocates only the result', but a clipped slot costs 3 allocations ([]rune, string, concatenation): testing.AllocsPerRun reports 3 for a 1 MiB slot (probe .../wp38-r2tq-k8m/probe/probe_clip_test.go via .../ov_clip.json). The []rune conversion also turns an invalid byte into U+FFFD only when the slot is clipped. Every message passes the result through %q, so the same authored byte renders differently by slot length: 64 code points give share slot "\xffaaa…", 65 give "�aaa…...". Stage G's clip (defaults/scalar.go:183-200) converts in both cases and stays consistent.
findings.fix: Return s[:i] + "...". range leaves i on a rune boundary and %q already escapes invalid bytes, so this is one allocation and gives the same rendering for every length. Update the doc and the TestClip row 'invalid UTF-8 in the kept prefix'. Alternatively keep the conversion in both branches, as stage G does, and correct the allocation claim.

findings.issue: Two assertions are weak. (a) onRequestHeaders of Route 'twice' may be [q gl] or [gl q], but class order fixes [gl q] (cors before admission). (b) The 'listed' loop only checks positions of the Route-scope q entries it finds, so it passes when the Route's q entry is missing. Mutant C01 drops a Route entry that re-lists a Gateway Policy (if it.entry.Replaces == it.entry.Policy { continue } before appending to routeEntries). It survives -run TestRepeatedEntries and is killed only by the fuzz seeds.
findings.fix: Assert exactly [gl q]. For 'listed', assert exactly one Route-scope q entry in onRequestHeaders at Position 0, and Removed == [{q q replaced-by q}].

WP-38 round 2 review, lens: tests and code quality. All scoped checks pass:
- go build and go vet
- go test -race -count=1 -cover -shuffle=on: 100.0% coverage
- CGO_ENABLED=0 go test
- -race -count=3 -cpu=1,2,4, and a stress run of -race -count=8 -cpu=4,2
- Go 1.26.8 floor with GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2
- bin/golangci-lint run: 0 issues; golangci-lint fmt --diff: empty; go run ./internal/tool/repocheck: exit 0
- FuzzPrecedenceInvariants: 45 s, 102k execs, pass (run in a scratch module copy so no corpus could be written into the repository)
- BenchmarkResolve (routes=5000) and BenchmarkRows run

The round-1 slot fix is complete for slots. Interning by id, clipping in the RZ-CFG-018 and RZ-CFG-019 messages, Rows escaping, the zero Resolver and the in-unit clock read all hold. My own mutants on that code (intern by name, maxQuoted 63, missing "...", Rows field and ordering mutants) are killed, as are 45 further mutants across resolve, locate, rows, work and parallel. No package file was modified; every probe ran through go test -overlay from /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp38-r2tq-k8m/.

One major finding: the round-1 byte-charging class is incomplete. Reference names (PolicyRef.name, RouteUpstream.name, CompositionStep.upstream) have no length bound. Stage I hashes and compares them per occurrence as one work unit each. With 4 unresolved 12 MiB references, inside every default limit, a worker goes 6.5 to 21 ms between two yield-timer reads, against 100 µs. That breaks the documented promise in work.go and Options.Now, and no contract request covers it.

Four minor findings:
- Two test gaps shown by surviving mutants, each with a probe that fails under the mutant: removal memo key injectivity, and the exact size of built Phases when a Route removes from and adds to the same Phase.
- clip's doc says it allocates only the result, but it allocates 3 times, and it renders an invalid byte differently depending on slot length.
- Two weak assertions in TestRepeatedEntries.

findings.where: internal/config/schemaview/work.go:29-37 (Options.MaxDiagnostics doc); mapping.go:322-330 (mapper.visit/locate per error); validate.go:120-127 (mapErrors keeps the whole jsonschema error tree alive while mapping); 11 req 17; 01 req 6
findings.issue:
Stage F's peak heap grows by about 1 KB per validation error, and the diagnostic cap does not limit it. This breaks the loader memory bound callers rely on (11 req 17: below 4x the source) and the package's own promise that a resource never stops the process ("a ruralzd reload keeps its active Revision").

Repro: probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp35r2int/probe_mem_test.go, run with `go test -count=1 -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp35r2int/overlay_mem.json -run TestProbeErrorMemory -v ./internal/config/schemaview/`. Input: a JSON Gateway whose one listener has `hostnames: [1,1,1,...]`, validated with ValidateWith(Options{MaxDiagnostics: 10}). Observed (11 diagnostics returned each time):
- n=100,000: 200,151-byte source, 83 MB peak heap (440x the source), 0.74 s
- n=400,000: 413 MB (542x), 2.7 s
- n=1,000,000: 2,000,151-byte source, 1,034 MB peak heap (542x), 8.0 s, 1.77 GB allocated

The split probe (overlay_mem2.json, TestProbeErrorMemorySplit) shows where it goes at 400,000 errors. The jsonschema/v6 call alone peaks at 155 MB. The full ValidateWith peaks at 390 MB. So the package's own mapping more than doubles the library's peak: it keeps a step, pathNode, textNode and interned segment text for every error position, while the library's error tree is still referenced.

Only MaxSourceBytes bounds a JSON document, so extrapolated:
- a 64 MiB JSON document needs about 33 GB and minutes in one worker
- a YAML document at MaxDocumentTokens (about 500,000 elements) needs about 0.5 GB per worker, times W concurrent workers on a Node

The round-3 doc fix is incomplete. The doc says "Peak loader memory is what the hostile-input fixtures measure (OQ-configuration-model-18)", but those fixtures (11 req 17: 64 MiB + 1 byte, 20,001 resources, depth 65) all fail at stages A and B and never reach stage F. OQ-configuration-model-18 decides the nesting depth only. No owner decision records this per-error cost.
findings.fix:
Inside the package:
- Make the mapping's memory independent of the number of errors once the cap is reached. Before memoizing a location, resolve its node and source position along the existing trie without creating new steps or interning text. When (file, line, column, code) already sorts after m.bound, skip the error, so only candidates that can be kept are memoized.
- Release each visited cause, for example `e.Causes[i] = nil` after visiting it, so the library's error tree is freed while mapping. Peak memory is then the larger of the validator tree and the mapping, not their sum.
- Add a test that bounds mapping-retained memory, or a counter of memoized steps, by O(cap x depth) for 1,000,000 type errors at cap 10. Keep it deterministic, for example by counting steps or texts interned.
- Correct the MaxDiagnostics doc: nothing measures this cost today.

File a contract request for the part the library holds (about 0.4 KB per error):
- Extend the round-1 JSON token cap request (01 req 6: MaxDocumentTokens also for JSON documents) with these measurements.
- Add a hostile-input fixture class to 11 req 17: one validation error per node, at the YAML token cap and at the JSON source cap.

findings.issue: Compile's documented precondition is "idx must have been loaded from the same bytes". The meta test compiles the authoring view with the rendered view's index: `Compile(schema.AuthoringV1alpha1(), testView(t).Index())`. Secret marks, list types, dispatch and hint names for authoring-view errors then come from a different document than the one validated. The precondition is not needed for this: probe TestProbeAuthoringIndex (overlay_auth.json in the same scratch dir) shows `schemaidx.Load("ruralz/v1alpha1", schema.AuthoringV1alpha1())` and `Compile(authoring, authoringIdx)` both succeed.
findings.fix: Build authoringView from `schemaidx.Load("ruralz/v1alpha1", schema.AuthoringV1alpha1())`. Alternatively, either state in the Compile doc which mismatches are tolerated, or make Compile check more than the kind set (for example, compare the indexed document's digest).

findings.issue:
The comment says the message is "The wording of 01 req 25 and of overlay.CheckBase, which reports the same rule with the same code before stage F". The two texts differ:

- overlay.CheckBase (internal/config/overlay/merge.go:912): `$patch is valid only in overlays`
The same RZ-CFG-006 rule at the same path therefore reads differently depending on which stage reports it. One case where only stage F reports it is canonical content entering through FromResources, which skips stage D.
findings.fix: Either emit exactly the CheckBase message for `$patch`, or reword the comment to say the message ends with CheckBase's wording. Add a test that pins the chosen relation between the two.

result.summary:
WP-35 round 2, lens contracts and integration. Verdict: fix, because of one major finding.

What holds:
- **Checks:** tests pass with `-race` (86 s) and on the Go 1.26 floor (`GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8 GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 CGO_ENABLED=0 -shuffle=on`). `bin/golangci-lint` reports 0 issues. The JSON-Schema-Test-Suite run (`-tags integration`) has zero failures.
- **Imports** match architecture 1.2: diag, schemaidx, tree, api/schema and jsonschema/v6. Test-only imports of subst, profile and registry create no import cycle.
- **Inputs are not mutated:** the resource tree is never changed, and each returned path is a fresh slice.
- **Sort order:** randomized probes of tricky field names, keys and quoting, with and without positions, show the mapper's interned-text order always equals `diag.List.Sort`.
- **Cap contract:** at every cap k, `ValidateWith` returns exactly the first k+1 entries of the full sorted result. That is what `diag.Collector` needs to append RZ-CFG-001.
- **Determinism and secrets:** results are deterministic across repeated runs. No literal secret value appeared in any message or path.
- **No silent pass:** a 60 s probe fuzz (1.3 million executions) found no instance that jsonschema/v6 rejects while Validate returns no error diagnostic. Pipeline gating on "no error diagnostics" is therefore safe.
- **Duplicate keys:** first-member-wins is applied consistently in the instance, locate, member, Walk dispatch, checkLists, checkReserved and varsBelow.
- **Cross-stage contracts:** keyed-list key fields are all strings, so stage F's canonical-JSON key comparison cannot disagree with key-aware paths. Duplicates that appear only after host lower-casing are reported by stage G. The exported API (Embedded, Set.ValidateWith, Options.MaxDiagnostics and Yield, Served, View.Index) covers what WP-69 and the Environments loader need. `Embedded` costs about 100 ms per process.

Major finding: stage F's peak heap grows about 1 KB per validation error, whatever the cap.
- **Measured:** a 2 MB JSON Gateway with 1,000,000 hostname type errors takes 1,034 MB peak heap (542x the source) and 8 s, at a cap of 10.
- **Where it goes:** the package's own mapping retention more than doubles what the library itself needs.
- **Extrapolated:** a 64 MiB JSON document needs about 33 GB. This breaks the 11 req 17 bound (below 4x the source) and the package's promise that a ruralzd reload keeps its active Revision.
- **Doc claim is wrong:** the round-3 MaxDiagnostics doc says the hostile-input fixtures measure this, but those fixtures never reach stage F.

Minor findings:
- The meta test compiles the authoring view with the rendered view's index, which breaks Compile's documented precondition.
- A comment claims the `$patch` message has the same wording as overlay.CheckBase, but the two texts differ.

All probes ran through `go test -overlay` from /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp35r2int/ (probe_cap_test.go, probe_mem_test.go, probe_mem2_test.go, probe_auth_test.go, probe_fuzz_test.go). No repository file was modified.

findings.issue: FuzzValidate fails after about 35 s of fuzzing. Command, run in a scratch copy of the module because the fuzzer writes into testdata/fuzz: `go test -run '^$' -fuzz '^FuzzValidate$' -fuzztime 120s ./internal/config/schemaview/`. Failing input: `{"kind":"Gateway","00000000":{"0000":"0"},"spec":{"listeners":[{"name":0e0}]}}`. Smallest form: `{"kind":"Gateway","spec":{"listeners":[{"name":0.0}]}}`. Validate reports `spec.listeners[name=0.0].name: must be a string...`, but the zeroed twin reports the same finding at `spec.listeners[name=0]`. The cause is that keyed-list path elements carry the key literal as written. That covers schemaidx.ItemElem's diag.Keyed(key, k.Text), reached through memo.itemElem and Walk, and duplicateKeys' own diag.Keyed(key, k.Text) at validate.go:258. `{"name":0},{"name":-0.0}` also fails: the duplicate is reported at `[name=-0.0]` in one run and `[name=0]` in the other. Both properties that compare res with zr fail. I reproduced each one on the real tree with an overlay probe (scratchpad r2/probe/probe_test.go, TestProbeZeroKey, `go test -overlay <scratch>/overlay.json -run TestProbeZeroKey ./internal/config/schemaview/`): the zero property at line 91-93 and the smallest-grid property at line 94-98. Stage 11 nightly `make fuzz` runs each target for 15 m, so it fails every night. With zeroed() changed to keep numbers inside list-item members as written, FuzzValidate passed 300 s with no other failure. FuzzNumberBound passed 150 s.
findings.fix: Fix the class. zeroed() must leave as written every number that names a keyed entry. That is the key member, as Get resolves it, of an element of a map or orderedMap list; resolve it through the schema index the way ItemElem does, or compare the two results with keyed elements normalized. The rule must hold for both comparisons that use zr: the zero property and the smallest-grid property. Commit the crasher and the 0.0, -0, -0.0 and {0,-0.0} duplicate forms as f.Add seeds (01 test plan: each crasher becomes a committed seed). Add a named table test per form that fails on the current harness, then re-run fuzzing for at least FUZZTIME. If the owner wants paths that agree with duplicateKeys (0 and -0.0 count as one key but render as [name=0] and [name=-0.0]), file a contract request on WP-03 to render numeric keyed values canonically in ItemElem, and use the same text in duplicateKeys.

findings.issue: A member whose Value is a nil *tree.Node makes Validate panic in three places. The package accepts that shape elsewhere: instance converts it to null and records shadowed values only when non-nil, varsBelow and Walk's descend skip it, and TestInstance has a "nil member value" case. Probe TestProbeNilMemberValue, run via overlay on Gateway trees, gave: `metadata.labels: <nil>` -> nil pointer dereference at validate.go:384 (`pairs.Kind`, because m.member returned (nil, true)); a listener `{name: <nil>, port: 80, protocol: http}` -> panic in schemaidx.isKeyScalar via memo.itemElem (locate.go:217); duplicateKeys' `k.Kind` at validate.go:247 dereferences the same nil once the locate path does not panic first. The same shape at `port` or as a label value maps cleanly to "must be an integer" or "must be a string". Front ends and overlay compaction do not emit nil values, so I rate this minor. A panic in the mapping, unlike one in the validator, is not recovered, though.
findings.fix: Treat a nil member value as JSON null in every mapping path: have mapper.member, or each caller, check for nil before reading Kind (checkReserved, duplicateKeys). Guard memo.itemElem before it calls schemaidx.ItemElem with an entry whose key value is nil, or file a contract request on WP-03 for a nil guard in ItemElem/isKeyScalar. Add table cases (nil labels, nil keyed key, two nil keyed keys) that panic on the current code.

findings.issue: When the first entry's key node has no known position, the related "first entry at" location falls back to the resource start, because knownPos(prev, nil) has no fallback node. The diagnostic itself falls back to the second entry (knownPos(k, item)), and duplicateElements falls back to the list (knownPos(prev, c.Node)). Probe TestProbeRelatedFallback: two listeners at lines 10 and 20 whose `name: "a"` nodes have Pos{}. Output: `f.json:20:3 error RZ-CFG-005 Gateway/g spec.listeners[name=a]: duplicate entry: name "a" is already used by an earlier entry (first entry at f.json:1:3)`. The related location points at the resource start, not the first entry (01 req 34: related the first).
findings.fix: Record the first entry's item next to its key node (first map value {key, item}) and use knownPos(prev, prevItem) for the Related location. Add a test with position-less key nodes that asserts the related line equals the first entry's line.

result.summary:
I reviewed every source file of internal/config/schemaview (schemaview, validate, work, mapping, locate, paths, numbers, vocabulary, rawschema) and the vendored suite metadata, with an adversarial-input lens. Things I probed that held up:

- Secret non-echo across validator, uniqueness and path outputs (no set or key in the rendered view carries a secret).
- Determinism under map-ordered validator errors.
- No recursive $defs, so anyOf/oneOf cannot blow up exponentially.
- Message bounds: the only unquoted names in messages come from the schema.

I measured peak live heap at about 552 B per validation error (276 B per document byte for a list of integers where strings are expected). That matches the documented figures under OQ-configuration-model-18, so I did not report it again.

I modified no repository file. The probes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/r2/probe/ and the fuzzing ran in the module copy at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/r2/mod/.

findings.issue: The zero property added in round 1 is false for valid input. A zero literal that is not written in canonical form (0.0, -0, 0e5) and is used as a keyed-list key shows up in the key-aware path exactly as written (01 req 48; schemaidx.ItemElem and duplicateKeys use k.Text). zeroed rewrites that key to "0", so Validate(res) and Validate(&zr) render different paths and the fuzz target fails. The second comparison in the same class was changed in round 1 from rawValidate(small, res) to rawValidate(small, &zr), but it still compares against small.Validate(res), so it fails the same way. Reproduction: in a scratch copy of the package, add a FuzzValidate corpus file with the input {"apiVersion": "ruralz/v1alpha1", "kind": "Gateway", "metadata": {"name": "x"}, "spec": {"listeners": [{"name": 0.0, "port": "x", "protocol": "http"}]}}, then run `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=1 -run 'FuzzValidate/keyzero' ./internal/config/schemaview/`. Observed: "Validate() differs from Validate() with every zero written 0: ... spec.listeners[name=0.0].name: must be a string ... versus ... spec.listeners[name=0].name ...". The input [{"name": -0, ...}, {"name": 0e5, ...}] also fails, at [name=-0] versus [name=0] and [name=0e5] versus [name=0]. With the first check disabled, the second fails with "Validate() at the smallest grid differs from the literals as written" on the same paths. The committed seeds pass because none has a numeric keyed key, so stage 5 is green, but the nightly 15-minute fuzz shard (11 req 28) would report a false crasher.
findings.fix: Fix both comparisons between res and zr. (a) For the zero property, either have zeroed leave keyed-list key members alone (walk with v.idx.Walk and, for a keyed list, skip each item's key member), or compare the two lists only after normalizing each diag.ElemKeyed value that parses as a zero literal to "0". (b) Run the smallest-grid comparison on one tree: small.Validate(&zr, files) against rawValidate(small, &zr, files). Commit both reproducers as seeds under testdata/fuzz/FuzzValidate/, and add a table test of the normalization or zeroed helper for keyed keys 0.0, -0 and 0e5. Each must fail on the current fuzz_test.go.

findings.issue: The new zero branch ends with `return`, which leaves the whole fuzz function. When a is a zero, b is never parsed or checked. The new seed f.Add("0e99999999999999999999", "-0.0E-9223372036854775808") therefore never looks at its second literal, the -2^63 boundary zero it was added to cover. The same is true of every fuzzed pair whose first literal is a zero.
findings.fix: Use `continue` instead of `return` in the zero branch. vals[i] and subs[i] stay unset, so the pair comparison after the loop is skipped as it should be. Optionally add a seed with the zero second and a nonzero literal first.

findings.issue: step.find compares tok in full with each of up to fewSteps children of equal length, but memo.step charges only `compared + len(tok)`. The bytes of each equal-length child compared are never charged. memo.index's small-object scan, the sibling member of this class, charges len(k) for every equal-length name it compares, and the Options.Yield doc lists comparing one long token as a span charged with its bytes. Probe in a scratch copy: 8 sibling steps with 64 KiB tokens that differ only in the last byte. step(parent, last) charged 65,544 units while the comparisons read about 524,289 bytes, an 8x undercharge. This is reachable with 8 equal-length long typed-map keys that each have an error below them. TestTextCharges "token looked up" uses a single child and TestStepIndex uses 2-byte tokens, so neither can see it.
findings.fix: Have find also return the bytes it compared (len(c.tok) for each scanned child with len(c.tok) == len(tok), plus len(tok) for the map lookup), and charge that in memo.step. Add a TestTextCharges growth case with fewSteps equal-length long siblings (growth fewSteps*n) and a TestStepIndex case with long equal-length tokens.

findings.issue: Round 1 added a new Compile refusal (ErrSchema) for a view zero whose exponent lies outside int64. It is documented only in a comment inside newNumberModel. The exported Compile doc still lists only the 400-digit and period refusals, and the ErrSchema doc lists none of the number-model refusals (digits, period, zero exponent). The numbers.go header still says Compile refuses only views whose numbers need more than maxViewDigits digits, and the newNumberModel doc does not mention any error.
findings.fix: Name all three number-model refusals in ErrSchema's doc and in Compile's doc: more than maxViewDigits digits, a period of more than maxPeriodDigits digits, and a zero with an exponent outside int64. Update the numbers.go header sentence and the newNumberModel doc to match.

- **Minor:** the set (RFC 8785 bytes) and map (Go string order) sort rules are not pinned for strings that RFC 8785 escapes; two mutants survive.

Not reported:
- The null refusal inside the JSONSchemaDocument and the case-fold refusal are already filed as contract requests.
- Moving the deprecation check after materialize and moving the registry defaults after the schema visit change nothing, so those two mutants prove nothing.
- Taking the slot name from res.ID versus metadata.name never differs in the pipeline.

WP-37 round 2, adversarial review (hostile inputs and failure modes). I changed no repository file. The probes are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/rev37r2/probe{1,2,3,4}_test.go and run with `go test -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/rev37r2/overlay.json -run TestProbe -v ./internal/config/defaults/`. I fuzzed on a scratch copy of the module (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/rev37r2/mod), so no corpus file could land in testdata.

Baseline: `go test -race` passes, with 98.6% coverage in defaults and 98.2% in convert. `go vet`, `gofmt -l` and `bin/golangci-lint run` on both packages are clean. FuzzStageIdempotent, FuzzChunkedDecode and FuzzFinder each ran 150 s with no failure.

What I checked and found sound:
- The case-fold rule matches encoding/json. I read the Go 1.27.1 fold.go: it uses SimpleFold orbits, which is the same relation as strings.EqualFold and foldName.
- integerText holds at exponent extremes, and float underflow is accepted, consistent with encoding/json.
- The keeper's comparePaths agrees with Path.String ordering.
- The chunker's split rules give the same result as a whole decode.
- Normalization is idempotent.
- The rules for nulls, nil nodes and invalid UTF-8 report each failure once.
- Messages quote no secret values. Secret fields hold only secretRef, and every quoted value goes through strconv.Quote and clip.
- Panic and Goexit handling, and cancellation, behave as documented.

Nothing reachable in M1 with the default converters breaks a requirement. The six findings below are all minor. Two of them (1 and 5) need a buggy converter. Findings 2 and 3 need a non-empty lifecycle table, which is empty in M1. Finding 4 is reachable in M1 on runs with more than the cap of diagnostics. Finding 6 needs duplicate identities, which stage C and the canonical decoder rule out in M1.

findings.issue: Each call to StripConversionData deletes only the first member named ruralz.io/conversion-data. If a converter result holds that member twice, the second one survives. Removing the first also removes the duplicate, so stage G's duplicate-name check never fires and the annotation reaches the hub and the canonical form with no diagnostic. This breaks 02 req 7 ('MUST NOT appear in the hub or canonical form'). It also breaks the Converter doc's promise that stage G fails a converter bug instead of letting it reach the canonical form. Probe TestProbeDupConversionData (probe1_test.go): a hub converter whose ToHub appends metadata.annotations {"ruralz.io/conversion-data":"a","ruralz.io/conversion-data":"b"}. Stage.Resource returned 0 diagnostics and the hub tree {"apiVersion":"ruralz/v1alpha1","kind":"Route","metadata":{"annotations":{"ruralz.io/conversion-data":"b"},"name":"r"},"spec":{...}}. Only a converter can produce this: the profile and the canonical decoder both reject duplicate names.
findings.fix: Delete every member with that name (repeat ann.Delete until it returns false, then drop an empty annotations object), or report the duplicate as RZ-CFG-005/007 before stripping. Add a test row with the annotation held twice, through both Registry.ToHub and Stage.Resource.

findings.issue: DeprecationsCounted builds every RZ-CFG-025 warning with no budget, and Stage.resource keeps only cap+1 of them afterwards (w.admit). Memory and time for warnings therefore grow with the input instead of the cap. This contradicts the Run doc ('The diagnostics held at any time are at most MaxDiagnostics+1 per worker'). The warnings also use up the resource's budget before normalization or decode can record any error. Probe TestProbeDeprecationsUnbounded (probe1_test.go): Lifecycle{Fields: {ruralz/v1alpha1: {"spec.upstreams[].weight"}}}, MaxDiagnostics 10, and a Route with 20,000 upstream entries that each set weight. DeprecationsCounted returned 20,000 diagnostics, each with its own path, while Resource returned 11. Latent in M1 because the table is empty.
findings.fix: Give DeprecationsCounted a budget, such as a max count or the worker's take function, so the walk stops building warnings after cap+1 while still counting its work. Test it with a lifecycle table whose warnings exceed the cap: assert how many it builds, and assert a later error still makes the resource fail.

findings.issue: nullsFilled scans the whole tree, then copies it, and reports each pass to count in a single call after that pass ends. The yield timer (w.charge) is therefore not read during two whole-tree passes. That contradicts work.go's bound: the timer is read every 256 units, and any longer gap is a single library call on one value. Probe TestProbeNullsFilledGap (probe2_test.go): lifecycle {"spec.timeout"}, a Route with 200,000 upstream entries and one nil member value. The count calls were [400008 400008 5 ...]: two charges of 400,008 units, each made only after a full pass. Only reachable with a non-empty lifecycle table.
findings.fix: Count as the work happens: call count per node, or every 256 nodes, inside scan and fill. Alternatively, avoid the copy by teaching the walk to read a nil member as null. Add a yield-gap test row (like TestYieldGapBytes) with a lifecycle table and a nil node.

findings.where: internal/config/defaults/keep.go:157 (keeper.add/prune), called from defaults.go:509 inside the worker
findings.issue: The keeper's appends and its prune (sorting 2(cap+1) entries with compareEntries) run in the worker goroutine. That work is outside the work-unit accounting and holds the keeper mutex, which blocks the other workers. The time between yield-timer reads can then far exceed both YieldAfter (100 µs) and the bound documented in work.go. Probe TestProbeKeeperAddTiming (probe4_test.go): 4 Routes with 10,005 upstream entries each, all "weight": null, default cap. The add for resource 0 took 11.6 ms and resource 1's add, which pruned 20,002 entries, took 28.2 ms. Probe TestProbeYieldGapKeeper: Run with 1 worker and Options.Now recording real time. The longest gap between two timer reads was 12.8 to 13.5 ms. Reachable in M1 on any run that hits the cap.
findings.fix: Charge the keeper's work to the worker: pass w to add, charge one unit per entry appended or compared, and charge each comparison in prune through a comparator that reads the timer. Or merge the sorted per-resource lists incrementally instead of sorting 2n entries at once. Document this in work.go and add a test of the yield gap with the keeper.

findings.issue: Stage F never validates the converted hub tree, and stage G checks only the shapes the Converter doc lists (null, nil, duplicate name, invalid UTF-8, number grammar, non-object). Other converter defects pass silently into the hub and the canonical form. Probe TestProbeConverterLeak (probe3_test.go): a hub converter adds spec.backends [] to a Route, whose RouteSpec is closed. Result: 0 diagnostics, and the hub tree holds "backends". Probe TestProbeConverterIdentity: a converter rewrites kind to Upstream and metadata.name to other. Result: 0 diagnostics, and hub.Resource Route/r is returned while its Tree and Object say Upstream/other. Enum and pattern violations decode into string fields unchecked in the same way. Latent in M1, where only the identity converter exists.
findings.fix: After a successful ToHub, check that kind and metadata.name still equal res.ID (RZ-CFG-007). For a non-hub apiVersion, also check that closed hub objects hold only declared members, or run the hub schema validator on the converted tree. Otherwise, narrow the Converter doc to say what is not checked, and file a contract request for the pipeline to re-validate converted trees. Add one test per defect shape.

findings.issue: Run drops a resource whose identity repeats an earlier one, silently and depending on input order. hub.NewBundle keeps the first by input order, Run reports no diagnostic, and it returns a non-nil Bundle. Probe TestProbeDuplicateIdentity (probe3_test.go): two Route/r resources (a.json with upstream a, b.json with upstream b) in input order [b, a]. With 1 and with 2 workers, the Bundle held 1 resource, from b.json, and there were 0 diagnostics. Not reachable through Load (stage C) or canonical decode (which rejects duplicates) in M1, but a FromResources producer in M2 would get no signal.
findings.fix: Have Run detect a duplicate ResourceID before building the Bundle and fail. Stage C owns the code, so either raise a programmer-error panic or file a contract request for which code to report. At minimum, state the uniqueness precondition in Run's doc and test it.

findings.where: internal/config/defaults/normalize.go:560-597 (number, checkNumber; free-content numbers are only range-checked, never brought to their canonical value), decode.go:224-231 (appendJSON writes the literal into Policy.Spec.Config and the typed configs); 02 req 34 ('Equal digests mean equal effective behavior on every Node that accepts them'), 02 req 20 and R-47 (FromResources), 04 req 55 ('A Revision whose digest equals the active one is a no-op')
findings.issue:
Stage G keeps the authored number literal in hub.Resource.Tree, in Policy.Spec.Config (json.RawMessage) and in the typed config. The canonical form, and so the Revision digest, holds the ECMAScript form of the literal's double. When two literals round to the same double but have different exact values, they get one digest but behave differently. In M1 the consumer that sees this is validation.json-schema (WP-51): jsonschema/v6 compares numbers exactly with big.Rat (validator.go:518-548).

Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/rev37c/probe3_test.go, run with `go test -count=1 -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/rev37c/overlay3.json -run TestProbeDigestBehavior -v ./internal/config/defaults/`. It runs stage F and stage G on two validation.json-schema Policies whose config is {"schema":{"type":"number","exclusiveMaximum":X}}, with X = 0.3 and X = 0.30000000000000001. Observed:
- The canonical bytes are equal (one digest).
- The typed Schema is {"exclusiveMaximum":0.3,...} for the first and {"exclusiveMaximum":0.30000000000000001,...} for the second.
- jsonschema/v6 with request body 0.3: the first source rejects it, the second accepts it.
- The second Policy after canonical Encode, Decode and stage G again (LKG boot or handover): the schema becomes {"exclusiveMaximum":0.3} and the body is rejected.

So one Revision behaves differently on a Node that loaded the source and on a Node that booted from its Last-Known-Good. An edit from 0.3 to 0.30000000000000001 is also a reload no-op (same digest) on a running Node, but it takes effect after a restart from source.

probe5_test.go (overlay5.json) shows the other members of the class, all accepted by stages F and G:
- Underflow: "minimum": 1e-400. The hub keeps 1e-400 and the canonical form writes 0, because jsonval.CheckNumber reads underflow as zero.
- An integral float above 2^53 at a number position: 9007199254740993.0. The hub keeps it and the canonical form writes 9007199254740992.
- Excess digits: "const": 0.30000000000000001, written as 0.3.

The class covers every free-content position: the JSONSchemaDocument value, undeclared members of +ruralz:open configs, plugin configs and Plugin configSchema. It also covers the spec.config RawMessage text that Filter factories decode.
findings.fix:
Make the hub carry exactly the value the digest covers, in Normalize, after the range check, at every number node. Choose one of two options and record it.

(a) Rewrite the text to jsonval.AppendCanonicalNumber's form. Keep KindFloat for non-integer-only positions, and make the range rule key on the node kind rather than on text without '.eE'. Otherwise an output such as 1e20, rewritten to 100000000000000000000, would fail the range rule when stage G re-reads it as authored content, and idempotence would break.

(b) Report RZ-CFG-005 for a literal whose exact decimal value differs from the value of its canonical form, for example "number 0.30000000000000001 has more precision than the canonical form keeps; write 0.3". This accepts 0.1, 1.50 and 1e2, and rejects 0.30000000000000001, 1e-400 and 9007199254740993.0.

With either option, add one table test per class member: excess digits, underflow, an integral float beyond 2^53, and each free position (JSONSchemaDocument, open-config member, plugin config). Each test runs canonical Encode, Decode and stage G again, and requires the typed config, the RawMessage and a jsonschema/v6 verdict to be equal before and after. File a contract request amending 02 req 16 and 18 ('numbers are carried as literals' / 'numbers per R-16') with the chosen rule, citing 02 req 34.

findings.where: internal/config/defaults/normalize.go:517-597 (scalar, byteSizeMessage, number, checkNumber), 638-721 (set and keyed duplicates), 345-349 (invalid UTF-8), decode.go:364-370 (locator.fail); 01 req 29; compare internal/config/schemaview/mapping.go:371-405 and validate.go:255-266
findings.issue:
Stage E records the substituted variables in tree.Node.Vars so that a refused value 'fails naming the variable' (01 req 29). Stage F does this for every value it refuses, including both keys of a duplicate. Stage G never reads Vars, so its RZ-CFG-005 findings about substituted values do not name the variable.

Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/rev37c/probe4_test.go (overlay4.json, -run TestProbeSubstitutedNamed) runs subst, then schemaview, then Stage.Resource:
- T=99x: stage F reports 'must be a Go duration such as 50ms; variable "T" was substituted into the value'.
- T=9999999h: stage G reports 'duration "9999999h" is out of range: ...' with no variable.
- S=8Pi in limits.maxRequestBodyBytes: 'integer 9007199254740992 is outside the I-JSON range ...' with no variable.
- hosts ["${A}","${B}"] with X.example and x.example: 'duplicate element "x.example" in a set after normalization', where stage F's equivalent message names both the key's and the earlier key's variables.
findings.fix: When the reported node, or for duplicates the key and the earlier key, carries Vars, append the same clause stage F writes ('; variable "T" was substituted into the value', at most 4 names, never a value). Do this for every stage G RZ-CFG-005 about a value: the duration overflow and syntax messages, the ByteSize message, the integer and double range messages, the invalid number and invalid UTF-8 messages, set and keyed duplicates after normalization, and the locator's decode failures. Add a table test per message through subst, schemaview and stage G, as TestSubstitutedInvalidUTF8 does.

findings.where: internal/config/convert/convert.go:73-101 (Converter doc), 149-157 (Registry concurrency claim); consumers: defaults.Stage.Run (concurrent ToHub), WP-58 render --api-version (02 req 53, partial overlay files)
findings.issue:
The Converter contract is wrong or incomplete for two of its callers.

(a) It says 'A converter's result holds each member name once per object, with no null and no nil node' for every document. Partial documents legitimately hold null: an overlay null removes a member (01 req 25, CM Overlays). render --api-version converts overlay files unmerged with partial=true. An M3 spoke converter that follows the doc would drop or reject those nulls, and the rewritten overlay would stop removing the field, which changes the rendered Revision that 02 req 53 compares.

(b) Registry is documented as safe for concurrent use, and Stage.Run calls Registry.ToHub from several workers at once. The Converter interface never requires an implementation to be safe for concurrent use, so a stateful converter passed as Options.Converters would race.
findings.fix: Scope the no-null and unique-name rule to whole resources (partial false). State that a partial document keeps authored nulls and $patch entries as they are, apart from renamed or moved fields. Add 'A Converter must be safe for concurrent use: Registry and stage G call it from several goroutines' to the interface doc. Add a FuzzConversionRoundTrip seed (or a table case) for an overlay patch whose object holds a null member beside a $patch entry, converted with partial=true through the identity and the test spoke.

result.summary:
I reviewed WP-37 round 2 for contracts and integration: internal/config/defaults and internal/config/convert, checked against the committed contracts (hub, diag, tree, schemaidx, registry, canonical) and the callers WP-58, WP-69 and WP-78. Verdict: fix, with one major finding and two minor ones.

**What holds:**
- Imports match architecture 1.2 and 1.3.
- The exported API covers what the pipeline and render need: Stage, New, Run, Resource and HubIndex, plus Registry with Convert, ToHub, FromHub, Served, CheckServed and Deprecations.
- hub.Resource is filled per the committed hub.go: Tree, Object, Config, Labels and Annotations without the conversion-data annotation, and Source.
- Diagnostics are capped at cap+1 for diag.Collector.
- Panics are re-raised on the caller.
- Build, vet and race tests pass. golangci-lint reports 0 issues. Tests pass on go1.26.8 with GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2.

**Probes** (all in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/rev37c, run through go test -overlay; nothing in the repository changed):
- R-47 holds for the example Bundle: stage G, the real canonical Encode, Decode, stage F and stage G again give identical canonical bytes (probe1_test.go).
- R-47 also held for every input the fuzzer generated: a 2-minute fuzz of the same round trip (probe2_test.go, run in a scratch copy of the module, about 2.1 million executions) found no failure.

**Major:** stage G keeps number literals in the hub (the Tree, spec.config and the typed configs), while the digest covers the literal rounded to a double. Two literals that round to the same double get one digest but behave differently.
- probe3_test.go: a validation.json-schema Policy with exclusiveMaximum 0.3 and one with 0.30000000000000001 produce equal canonical bytes. jsonschema/v6 accepts body 0.3 under the second schema, but rejects it after a Last-Known-Good round trip.
- This breaks 02 req 34. It also makes such an edit a reload no-op on a running Node (same digest).
- Other members of the same class: underflow such as 1e-400, and 9007199254740993.0 at a number position (probe5_test.go).

**Minor:**
- Stage G's RZ-CFG-005 messages never name substituted variables. Stage F does this per 01 req 29 (probe4_test.go).
- The Converter interface doc forbids null even in partial overlay documents, which render --api-version converts. It also never requires a Converter to be safe for concurrent use, though Stage.Run calls it from several workers.

I could not see this round's contractRequests, so I left out spec-text items that may already be filed, such as 02 req 24's statement that the loader rejects invalid UTF-8 as RZ-CFG-001.

findings.where: internal/config/subst/walk.go:294-305 (keyWarning reports at w.here(diag.Field(m.Key))); internal/config/subst/meter.go:248-257 (itemElem names a string set element diag.Item(item.Text) and a keyed entry diag.Keyed(key, k.Text)); walk.go:561-620 (detect, detectRuns and warn report at w.here()); review_test.go:440-470 TestKeyCredentials (checks only Message+Hint); 01 J row 013 ("The message names the detector, never the value"); 01 req 49 and 56
findings.issue: Every RZ-CFG-013 warning for a credential-shaped literal prints the credential it detected, through the diagnostic path, whenever the credential is in a mapping key, a set element, or a keyed-list key field. The keyWarning doc says the warning names "the detector, never the key", but its path is the key itself. TestKeyCredentials checks only Message and Hint, so it passes anyway. The path is part of the text form (01 req 49), of the JSON form, and of the Node's warn log line (01 req 56 logs `path`). So the warning that exists to keep credentials out spreads them into CLI and CI output and into Node logs. For RZ-CFG-012 the 01 test plan already requires the literal to be absent from text, JSON and logs. Reproduction: `go test -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/probe2/overlay.json -run TestZZCredentialInPath -count=1 ./internal/config/subst/` (probe file /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/probe2/leak_test.go) fails with these lines: `r.yaml:1:81 warning RZ-CFG-013 Route/r metadata.labels.AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP: credential-shaped mapping key (AWS access key ID) ...`; `r.yaml:1:121 warning RZ-CFG-013 Policy/c spec.config.allowOrigins[item=https://user:pass@example.com]: credential-shaped value (URL with a password) ...`; `r.yaml:1:125 warning RZ-CFG-013 Upstream/u spec.endpoints[address=https://user:pass@example.com].address: credential-shaped value (URL with a password) ...`. A plugin-config key `Bearer abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz` and a JWT audience set element `AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP` leak the same way.
findings.fix: Fix the whole class in subst. Give every RZ-CFG-013 credential warning (keyWarning, detect, detectRuns, headerValue via warn) a path that cannot hold the matched text. For a key warning, report at the parent object's path and keep the key's location. For a value warning, write the warned scalar's own set-element element `[item=...]`, a small composite set element `[item={...}]` that holds it, and a keyed-entry element `[<key>=...]` whose key field is the warned scalar, by index (`[i]`). config/canonical already names large set elements this way. Location stays the value position (J row 013). Add one table row per class member (mapping key in labels, annotations and free content; string set element; composite set element; keyed-list key field, such as endpoints address and headers set name). Each row asserts the credential is absent from d.AppendText and from the JSON form, and each must fail on the current code. Correct the keyWarning doc and the TestKeyCredentials doc. File a contract request against 01 req 48 and the J row 013: a diagnostic of any stage (message and path) never repeats a detected credential, because stage F diagnostics inside such an entry still print the key through the general path rule.

findings.where: internal/config/subst/walk.go:358-367 (the malformed branch of scalar reports RZ-CFG-005 and the secret-like names, but never check()'s RZ-CFG-010); fuzz_test.go:291 (oracle pins errs == 1 for malformed text); 01 req 27 ("one diagnostic per occurrence"); CM "Validation and diff semantics" ("report every error in one run")
findings.issue: A scalar that holds a malformed ${ reports RZ-CFG-005 alone among errors. A well-formed expression of an undefined variable in the same scalar gets no RZ-CFG-010. Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/probe/subst_probe_test.go cases "undefined then malformed" (prefixRoute("${UNDEF} ${1X}")) and "malformed then undefined" (prefixRoute("${1X} ${UNDEF}")). Run with -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/probe/overlay_subst.json -run TestZZProbe -v. Each gives only `RZ-CFG-005 ... malformed substitution (a variable name matches ...)`, and no RZ-CFG-010 for UNDEF. The secret-like name warning was made independent of the scalar's other error on purpose (TestMalformedSecretNames, package doc). The undefined-variable error was not, and no document records that decision. The author fixes ${1X}, runs again, and only then learns that UNDEF is undefined.
findings.fix: Option (a), matching 01 req 27 and the CM: in the malformed branch, read the text leniently, as secretNames does. Report RZ-CFG-010 (with its hint) for each well-formed expression without a default whose variable is undefined. A nested-default opening such as `${A:-${B}}` is read as secretNames reads it, or skipped if the owner prefers. Add rows for undefined before and after the malformed ${, and update the FuzzSubst oracle (errs == 1 + lenient undefined count). Option (b): record that a malformed scalar takes RZ-CFG-005 alone in the package doc and the Apply doc, with a contract request against 01 req 27. Option (b) still conflicts with the CM's "report every error in one run", so (a) is preferred.

findings.where: internal/config/overlay/merge.go:555-559 (redispatched message); 01 req 25 last-but-one bullet ("`$patch` in a base document: RZ-CFG-006 (\"valid only in overlays\")")
findings.issue: This round correctly moved the redispatched base $patch to RZ-CFG-006. Its message is still "$patch from the base document is no longer inside a JSON Schema document after the overlay merge". It does not carry the text 01 req 25 gives for this code and rule ("valid only in overlays"), which CheckBase uses ("$patch is valid only in overlays"). The same base $patch therefore reads differently depending on which path found it.
findings.fix: Start the message with the spec text, for example "$patch is valid only in overlays: this base $patch is no longer inside a JSON Schema document after the overlay merge". Keep the hint and related location. Update the expected strings in TestRedispatchedBasePatch, TestRedispatchNested and TestUnresolvedDispatch.

result.summary:
WP-36 round 2, spec-conformance review. I checked 01 req 23-31 and the 01 J row for RZ-CFG-013 against the code. Most of it is implemented and tested: keyed and orderedMap merges, the {$patch: replace} reorder, delete entries, null removal, both ruralz.io/patch actions, RZ-CFG-008/030/007, RZ-CFG-005/006 directive errors, position keeping, the grammar and escapes, forbidden positions, re-typing, secret-like names, the detectors, and Escape.

All 7 findings of the previous round are verified fixed:
- settle reads the merged dispatch, with tests for class members (a)-(e).
- The redispatched base $patch now reports RZ-CFG-006.
- The literal tests and comments, the walk and subst package docs, and the paragraph rewrap are done.

Checks I ran:
- go test -race -cover: overlay 99.6%, subst 98.8%; also run with CGO_ENABLED=0 and -shuffle=on.
- go vet; bin/golangci-lint on both packages (0 issues); repocheck (clean).
- FuzzOverlay for 120 s, and FuzzSubst, FuzzScan, FuzzHints and FuzzDetectors for 60 s each, in a scratch copy of the repo: all pass.
- -overlay probes on the merge and substitution edge cases.

New findings:
- Major: RZ-CFG-013 credential warnings print the detected credential through the diagnostic path. This happens for mapping keys, set elements and keyed-list key fields, in the text form, the JSON form and the Node's log line. The code's own doc says \"never the key\", and the test checks only Message and Hint.
- Minor: a scalar that also holds a malformed ${ suppresses RZ-CFG-010 for its undefined variables, and no document records that decision.
- Minor: the redispatched RZ-CFG-006 message lacks the \"valid only in overlays\" text that 01 req 25 gives.

Not reported because already filed: unbounded path text. One long key above many diagnostics turns 1 MiB of input into about 1 GB of text across 1,000 diagnostics. WP-37 and WP-39 already filed this as contract requests against diag and schemaidx, naming overlay. No repository file was modified; the probes are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/probe and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/probe2.

findings.issue: The test is flaky. It asserts that runtime.MemStats.TotalAlloc grows by at most 4096 bytes across one clip(16 MiB) call, but TotalAlloc counts every goroutine, and allocations from the runtime or the test framework sometimes land inside that window and add about 5.7 to 6 KB. AGENTS.md forbids this ('Deterministic tests ... never assert ... without a margin proven under load'). Reproduced three ways: (1) `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=3000 -run TestClipBounded ./internal/config/convert/ ./internal/config/defaults/` failed once: 'deprecations_test.go:330: clip of 16 MiB = 67 bytes, allocating 5736; want 67 bytes and at most 4096'. (2) `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=300 -run TestClipBounded -cpu 1,4 ./internal/config/convert/ ./internal/config/defaults/` failed once in defaults: 'scalar_test.go:123: ... allocating 5960'. findings.issue:
The new metamorphic property in FuzzOverlay is false, so the fuzz target fails on valid inputs. The property says that removing an overlay member whose value is a null tree over a base scalar changes neither the result nor the diagnostics. Three classes of input break it. To reproduce, I added each pair as a seed in an overlay copy of fuzz_test.go and ran `go test -count=1 -run FuzzOverlay -overlay <ov.json> ./internal/config/overlay/`. Every seed failed with "a member holding nothing but removals over a base scalar changed the merge".
(a) A $patch key inside the null tree. nullTree treats `{"$patch":null}` as a removal, but the merge correctly reports it as a misplaced directive (RZ-CFG-005, 01 req 25). base `{"kind":"Route","spec":{"timeout":"5s"}}` with overlay `{"spec":{"timeout":{"$patch":null}}}` gives `[RZ-CFG-005 Route/x spec.timeout.$patch]` before the drop and `[]` after it. The nested form `{"spec":{"timeout":{"x":{"$patch":null}}}}` and the dispatch member `{"spec":{"type":{"$patch":null}}}` over a cors Policy fail the same way.
(b) The patch annotation inside the dropped value. The path skip only matches the member `metadata.annotations["ruralz.io/patch"]` itself, not a parent that holds it. base `{"kind":"Route","metadata":{"annotations":"x"}}` with overlay `{"metadata":{"annotations":{"ruralz.io/patch":null}}}` loses `RZ-CFG-005 unsupported ruralz.io/patch value null`.
(c) A replace annotation. With ruralz.io/patch: replace, the overlay spec is kept even when it holds nothing but removals. base `{"kind":"Route","spec":"x"}` with overlay `{"metadata":{"annotations":{"ruralz.io/patch":"replace"}},"spec":{"a":null}}` merges to `spec:{}`, but after the drop the result has no spec.
In all three cases the merge follows 01 req 25 and its documented semantics; the oracle is what is wrong. A 300 s fuzz run did not reach these inputs. Each one is a few bytes away from an existing seed, so the nightly fuzz job can hit any of them at random.
findings.fix: Fix all three classes in the oracle. nullTree returns false for any member keyed $patch, at any depth. dropRemovals skips any member whose subtree holds the ruralz.io/patch key (or the whole metadata.annotations path), and skips the root spec when the overlay root carries a ruralz.io/patch annotation. Add the three failing pairs above, plus the nested and spec.type variants, as FuzzOverlay seeds so each class has a regression seed that fails without the fix.

findings.issue: When the stand-in changes the dispatch, settle clones and normalizes every overlay composite that replaces a base scalar, before the merge and before any diagnostic is reported. That includes members no dispatch rule tests, although settle's own comment says the dispatch reads the same whatever the merge leaves in them. So for this shape the pre-pass bypasses the diagnostic-budget stop that TestDiagnosticBudget pins: "a document with many more occurrences allocates no more". The new row "misplaced $patch in values replacing base scalars" misses this because its dispatch does not change, so settle returns at `same`. Probe: I added a producer to an overlay copy of budget_test.go with base spec {type:"cors", m0..mk:"s"} and overlay spec {type:{a:1}, m0..mk:{x:{$patch:1,a:1}}}. Running `go test -run 'TestDiagnosticBudget/PROBE' -overlay ...` printed "200829 allocations for 10050 occurrences, 321562 for 20100: the walk goes on past the budget". The cost stays linear in the input and the clones are short-lived garbage, so this is a wasted pre-pass, not a memory blow-up.
findings.fix: Run the trial only for members the dispatch may read: the declared properties that selectOf's proxy collects, or the tested members. Replace clone+normalize with a non-allocating predicate that walks the overlay value with normalize's rules and stops at the first value that would remain; pin it against normalize(clone) != nil with a differential or fuzz test. Then add this producer to budgetProducers, plus a variant whose single dispatch-member value holds k misplaced $patch members.

result.summary:
I reviewed WP-36 round 2 by reading overlay.go, merge.go, meter.go and selection.go in full, the new and changed overlay and subst tests, and subst.go, walk.go, scan.go, detect.go and meter.go; retype.go, environ.go and hint.go I only skimmed. All probes went through go test -overlay, and fuzzing ran in a scratch copy (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/r2/copy), so no repository file changed.

Checks:
- go build and go vet: clean.
- go test -race -count=1 -cover -shuffle=on -cpu 4: overlay passes (99.6% coverage, 204 s); subst passes alone (98.8%, 242 s) but timed out at 10 minutes when it shared the 4 CPUs with my other runs (minor 3).
- CGO_ENABLED=0 go test: passes (23 s per package).
- bin/golangci-lint run: 0 issues. golangci-lint fmt --diff: empty. repocheck: passes.
- FuzzOverlay ran 300 s and FuzzSubst 240 s with no failure, though FuzzOverlay's new property is false (the major finding).

The round 2 fixes hold where I tested them:
- settle, the redispatch code RZ-CFG-006 and the reworked related location behave as the engineer reported.
- Settle mutants are all killed: no shortcut, inverted trial, no quiet, no budget check, restore skipped, never run, wrong order.
- Mutants of the subst header literal rule are all killed: last-run framing, default counted as source, last expression decides, scheme on every run, empty value, shown name, no framed shortcut.

Open findings:
- **Major:** the new metamorphic property in FuzzOverlay (dropRemovals and nullTree) is false for three input classes: a $patch key inside the null tree, a parent of the ruralz.io/patch annotation, and a spec under ruralz.io/patch: replace. I reproduced each one with seeds; the target fails on inputs where the merge itself is correct.
- **Minor 1:** settle's trial clones and normalizes every overlay composite that replaces a base scalar, even members no rule tests. Once the dispatch changes, this skips the diagnostic-budget stop (200829 against 321562 allocations).
- **Minor 2:** two mutants of the new related-location rule survive (I give the rows that kill them), the row "no member a rule tests" uses a member a boolean rule tests, and the string-constant limit is not documented.
- **Minor 3:** the race runs take a large share of the default 10-minute timeout.

findings.where: internal/config/precedence/resolve.go:372-380 (attachList, the single RZ-CFG-018 producer for the Gateway list, every Route list and every Upstream list); testdata/fixtures/018-*/want.txt; 01-config-load.md req 39 J row 018

findings.where: internal/config/precedence/work.go:234-283 (one keeper per worker, kept for the whole call), resolve.go:243-258 (merged only after every Route), precedence.go:119-136 and 277-282 (doc: 'cap times the worker count')
findings.issue: The round-3 B1 fix (diagnostic cap, 01 req 50) is incomplete once there is more than one worker. Each worker keeps up to MaxDiagnostics+1 findings across all of its Routes, and admits() compares only against that worker's own heap root. So the findings held, and the findings built and then dropped, grow with the worker count instead of staying at the cap. When workers >= Routes the cap holds back nothing. The CLI passes GOMAXPROCS and the Node passes GOMAXPROCS/2 (02 req 78). Input: the B1 probe shape, P=1000 auth.upstream-oauth2 Policies and R=400 Routes each listing all 1000 (RZ-CFG-020 at Route scope, 400,000 findings), with positioned trees (positioned()). Probes /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp38-advr2-q4z/probe_cap_test.go, run with `go test -count=1 -run 'TestProbeCapPerWorker|TestProbeCapRetained' -v -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp38-advr2-q4z/overlay_cap.json ./internal/config/precedence/`. Findings held after the Route forEach, with live heap growth: W=1: 10,001 (6 MiB); W=4: 40,004 (25 MiB); W=16: 120,005 (74 MiB); W=64: 175,004 (109 MiB); W=400: 400,000 (257 MiB), more than the 194 MiB measured before the B1 fix. TotalAlloc of Run: 50, 99, 259, 444 and 1,133 MiB. The canonical form of this Bundle is about 7 MB, so from about 8 workers up stage I's findings alone exceed the 4x-canonical peak target of 02 req 78. The fix report's '5 MiB retained' holds only at W=1. Stage G does better (defaults.go:398-430): a per-resource buffer and one shared keeper, holding fewer than 2x the cap.
findings.fix: Bound the findings across workers, not per worker: give each work unit its own small keeper; at the end of the unit, merge its sorted findings into one shared keeper under a mutex and reset the unit's buffer, as stage G does. Let admits() also reject against the shared keeper's root head (file, line, column, code), read under the same lock at the start of the unit or published through an atomic snapshot, so a finding that sorts after the global cap+1 is never built. The bound becomes keep + workers x (findings of one unit), and the result stays deterministic because the ranks are unchanged. Change TestDiagnosticCapBoundsMemory to run at workers 1, 4 and R (>= Routes); assert that the sum of keeper peaks is at most keep + workers x P and that Run's TotalAlloc does not grow with the worker count beyond a stated margin. Correct the MaxDiagnostics, Resolve and package docs.

findings.where: internal/config/precedence/work.go:40-47 (claim); resolve.go:222-231 addKeys, :302-303 and :314 selectOne b.Get, :357 attachList sels lookup, :474 exclusion byName lookup, :752-778 legOrder; locate.go:143 and :148-156 listLoc.entry
findings.issue: The round-1 fix charges slot text by bytes (siteSlotIntern, 1+len/byteUnit) but not the other authored text of unbounded length that stage I hashes and compares: reference names. The schema gives PolicyRef.name, RouteUpstream.name and CompositionStep.upstream no maxLength, and stage I still runs when references do not resolve (02 req 40). Each such name costs one work unit however long it is, so the documented promise breaks: work.go says 'the time between two reads of the timer stays bounded', and Options.Now says 'stage I shares the processor with live traffic during activation'. Exact input: one Route whose spec.policies holds 4 unresolved names of 12 MiB each (48 MiB, inside the 64 MiB source cap); the same for spec.upstreams with 4 such names, and for spec.excludePolicies with 4 such names against a Gateway of 16 Policies. Command: `go test -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp38-r2tq-k8m/ov_gap.json -count=1 -run TestProbeRefGap -v ./internal/config/precedence/` (probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp38-r2tq-k8m/probe/probe_refgap_test.go). Observed with YieldAfter 100 µs over 4 runs, longest gap between two Options.Now reads: 13-21 ms for policies (24 clock reads in the whole Run), 9-20 ms for upstreams (6 reads), 6.5 ms for exclusions (36 reads); the short-name baseline is 7-135 µs. Class members, each an uncharged O(len) hash or compare per occurrence: addKeys inserting into s.sels (Gateway, Route and Upstream lists); selectOne s.b.Get for the Policy and for the Plugin reference; the attachList sels lookup; the route() exclusion lookup in gateway.byName; the listLoc.entry name compare and its byName index; legOrder's sort comparisons, seen map and s.upstreams lookup for spec.upstreams and composition steps. Not covered by the round-1 deviation (slots only, with a slot-length contract request), and no contract request covers reference lengths. (Related but separate: the adversarial minor on bulk charges after O(n) passes falsifies the same work.go claim.)
findings.fix: Stage F bounds every metadata.name to 63 bytes, so a longer reference can never resolve. At every member site, treat a reference name longer than 63 bytes as unresolved (skip it as sel==nil or missing) before any map operation or comparison. Charging 1+len/byteUnit at each site is weaker: it still leaves one uninterruptible hash per name. Add one TestWorkCharged/TestSlotWorkOnce-style row per site asserting that work units and clock reads do not grow with a reference's length above 63 bytes, and prove each row against the current code with -overlay. Correct the work.go and Options.Now claims. File a contract request to give the x-ruralz-ref string fields (PolicyRef.name, RouteUpstream.name, CompositionStep.upstream, PolicySpec.plugin) maxLength 63 and the RFC 1123 pattern in pkg/config/v1alpha1.
