minors.issue: If a work unit ends through runtime.Goexit (for example a test oracle calling t.FailNow, or any injected Body or Now that does so), the pooled path silently returns a wrong result. recover() returns nil, so pool.run reports no panic; the worker goroutine exits and the other workers keep draining, so Run succeeds. Inline, the same call ends the caller's goroutine. Input: Policy az-exit of type authz.cel with rule "exit && request.body.x", plus cache, cors and ratelimit; Gateway [cors, rl]; Route [az-exit, cache]; Options.Body calls runtime.Goexit for a rule containing "exit" (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp38-advr2-q4z/probe_goexit_test.go with overlay_goexit.json). At workers 2 and 4: no error, no diagnostics, and the chain has no az-exit; with an honest oracle the same Bundle gives RZ-CFG-038 and az-exit in onRequestBody. The authorization Policy is dropped and the Bundle accepted. Class members: selectAll (the zero selection is taken as a valid entry with Policy "" and no Phases, and takes slot ""); attachUpstreams (a Now that Goexits leaves a silently empty leg); the Route forEach (results[i] stays nil, which panics with a nil dereference at s.chains[c.Route]). Options.Body's doc does not forbid Goexit; only the unexported forEach does. Sibling stage G handles this case (defaults.go:423-427, errGoexit).
minors.fix: In pool.run, set a done flag after fn returns. In the deferred function, treat 'not done and recover() == nil' as a unit failure carrying an errGoexit value with the stack, record the stop as for a panic, and raise it again in the caller for every worker count, as stage G does. Document this on Options.Body and Options.Now. Add one test per member (Body in selectAll, Now in attachUpstreams, Now in the Route forEach), each at workers 1 and 4, each failing without the fix.

The parsed tree plus the typed hub resources hold 86 MiB; selectAll adds 63 MiB live, 309 B per absent reference. At 1,000,000 references it adds 295 MiB live (472 MiB TotalAlloc). A 64 MiB source (about 4M 16-byte references) therefore costs about 1.2 GB in stage I alone, for references it ignores.

minors.issue: The work.go doc says every input-length loop 'counts its elements at its own site, so the time between two reads of the timer stays bounded'. The number of resolvable Gateway Policies, which MaxResources caps at 20,000, bounds these passes, but each is still one stretch of up to about 20,000 elements (k log k for the sort) between two timer reads, against 256 elsewhere. (Related but separate: the code-lens major on uncharged reference-name lengths falsifies the same work.go claim.)

Collect the fate keys in a charged loop and sort them with slices.SortFunc and a charging comparator. findings.where: internal/config/schemaview/fuzz_test.go:89-99 (FuzzValidate: zero property at 91-93 and smallest-grid comparison at 94-98); zero_test.go:274 (zeroed); key text from schemaidx.ItemElem diag.Keyed(key, k.Text) via memo.itemElem/Walk and from duplicateKeys diag.Keyed(key, k.Text) at validate.go:258

findings.where: internal/config/schemaview/work.go:29-37 (Options.MaxDiagnostics doc); mapping.go:322-330 (mapper.visit/locate per error); validate.go:120-127 (mapErrors keeps the whole jsonschema error tree alive while mapping); 11 req 17; 01 req 6
findings.issue: Stage F's peak heap grows by about 1 KB per validation error, and the diagnostic cap does not limit it. This breaks the loader memory bound callers rely on (11 req 17: below 4x the source) and the package's own promise that a resource never stops the process ("a ruralzd reload keeps its active Revision"). Repro: probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp35r2int/probe_mem_test.go, run with `go test -count=1 -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp35r2int/overlay_mem.json -run TestProbeErrorMemory -v ./internal/config/schemaview/`. Input: a JSON Gateway whose one listener has `hostnames: [1,1,1,...]`, validated with ValidateWith(Options{MaxDiagnostics: 10}); 11 diagnostics are returned each time. n=100,000: 200,151-byte source, 83 MB peak heap (440x), 0.74 s. n=400,000: 413 MB (542x), 2.7 s. n=1,000,000: 2,000,151-byte source, 1,034 MB peak heap (542x), 8.0 s, 1.77 GB allocated. The split probe (overlay_mem2.json, TestProbeErrorMemorySplit) at 400,000 errors: the jsonschema/v6 call alone peaks at 155 MB, the full ValidateWith at 390 MB. So the package's mapping more than doubles the library's peak: it keeps a step, pathNode, textNode and interned segment text for every error position while the library's error tree is still referenced. Only MaxSourceBytes bounds a JSON document. Extrapolated: a 64 MiB JSON document needs about 33 GB and minutes in one worker; a YAML document at MaxDocumentTokens (about 500,000 elements) needs about 0.5 GB per worker, times W concurrent workers on a Node. The round-3 doc fix is incomplete: the doc says "Peak loader memory is what the hostile-input fixtures measure (OQ-configuration-model-18)", but those fixtures (11 req 17: 64 MiB + 1 byte, 20,001 resources, depth 65) all fail at stages A and B and never reach stage F. OQ-configuration-model-18 decides the nesting depth only, and no owner decision records this per-error cost.
findings.fix: Inside the package: (1) Make the mapping's memory independent of the number of errors once the cap is reached. Before memoizing a location, resolve its node and source position along the existing trie without creating new steps or interning text; when (file, line, column, code) already sorts after m.bound, skip the error, so only candidates that can be kept are memoized. (2) Release each visited cause (for example `e.Causes[i] = nil` after visiting it) so the library's error tree is freed while mapping; peak memory is then the larger of the validator tree and the mapping, not their sum. (3) Add a deterministic test that bounds mapping-retained memory, or a counter of memoized steps or interned texts, by O(cap x depth) for 1,000,000 type errors at cap 10. (4) Correct the MaxDiagnostics doc: nothing measures this cost today. File a contract request for the part the library holds (about 0.4 KB per error): extend the round-1 JSON token cap request (01 req 6: MaxDocumentTokens also for JSON documents) with these measurements; add a hostile-input fixture class to 11 req 17 (one validation error per node, at the YAML token cap and at the JSON source cap); and record the per-error bound, or the owner's acceptance of it, in OQ-configuration-model-18 or a new OQ row.

findings.where: internal/config/defaults/normalize.go:560-597 (number, checkNumber; free-content numbers are only range-checked, never brought to their canonical value), decode.go:224-231 (appendJSON writes the literal into Policy.Spec.Config and the typed configs); 02 req 34 ('Equal digests mean equal effective behavior on every Node that accepts them'), 02 req 20 and R-47 (FromResources), 04 req 55 ('A Revision whose digest equals the active one is a no-op')
findings.issue: Stage G keeps the authored number literal in hub.Resource.Tree, in Policy.Spec.Config (json.RawMessage) and in the typed config, while the canonical form, and so the Revision digest, holds the ECMAScript form of the literal's double. When two literals round to the same double but have different exact values, they get one digest but behave differently. In M1 the consumer that sees this is validation.json-schema (WP-51): jsonschema/v6 compares numbers exactly with big.Rat (validator.go:518-548). Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/rev37c/probe3_test.go, run with `go test -count=1 -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/rev37c/overlay3.json -run TestProbeDigestBehavior -v ./internal/config/defaults/`. It runs stage F and stage G on two validation.json-schema Policies whose config is {"schema":{"type":"number","exclusiveMaximum":X}}, with X = 0.3 and X = 0.30000000000000001. Observed: the canonical bytes are equal (one digest); the typed Schema is {"exclusiveMaximum":0.3,...} for the first and {"exclusiveMaximum":0.30000000000000001,...} for the second; jsonschema/v6 with request body 0.3 rejects it under the first source and accepts it under the second; the second Policy after canonical Encode, Decode and stage G again (LKG boot or handover) becomes {"exclusiveMaximum":0.3} and the body is rejected. So one Revision behaves differently on a Node that loaded the source and on a Node that booted from its Last-Known-Good, and an edit from 0.3 to 0.30000000000000001 is a reload no-op (same digest) on a running Node but takes effect after a restart from source. probe5_test.go (overlay5.json) shows the other class members, all accepted by stages F and G: underflow ("minimum": 1e-400; the hub keeps 1e-400 and the canonical form writes 0, because jsonval.CheckNumber reads underflow as zero); an integral float above 2^53 at a number position (9007199254740993.0; the hub keeps it and the canonical form writes 9007199254740992); excess digits ("const": 0.30000000000000001, written as 0.3). The class covers every free-content position: the JSONSchemaDocument value, undeclared members of +ruralz:open configs, plugin configs and Plugin configSchema, and the spec.config RawMessage text that Filter factories decode.
findings.fix: Make the hub carry exactly the value the digest covers, in Normalize, after the range check, at every number node. Choose one of two options and record it. (a) Rewrite the text to jsonval.AppendCanonicalNumber's form; keep KindFloat for non-integer-only positions, and make the range rule key on the node kind rather than on text without '.eE', otherwise an output such as 1e20, rewritten to 100000000000000000000, would fail the range rule when stage G re-reads it as authored content and idempotence would break. (b) Report RZ-CFG-005 for a literal whose exact decimal value differs from the value of its canonical form, for example "number 0.30000000000000001 has more precision than the canonical form keeps; write 0.3"; this accepts 0.1, 1.50 and 1e2, and rejects 0.30000000000000001, 1e-400 and 9007199254740993.0. With either option, add one table test per class member: excess digits, underflow, an integral float beyond 2^53, and each free position (JSONSchemaDocument, open-config member, plugin config). Each test runs canonical Encode, Decode and stage G again, and requires the typed config, the RawMessage and a jsonschema/v6 verdict to be equal before and after. File a contract request amending 02 req 16 and 18 ('numbers are carried as literals' / 'numbers per R-16') with the chosen rule, citing 02 req 34.

findings.issue: The test is flaky. It asserts that runtime.MemStats.TotalAlloc grows by at most 4096 bytes across one clip(16 MiB) call, but TotalAlloc counts every goroutine, and allocations from the runtime or the test framework sometimes land inside that window and add about 5.7 to 6 KB. AGENTS.md forbids this ('Deterministic tests ... never assert ... without a margin proven under load'). Reproduced three ways: (1) `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=3000 -run TestClipBounded ./internal/config/convert/ ./internal/config/defaults/` failed once: 'deprecations_test.go:330: clip of 16 MiB = 67 bytes, allocating 5736; want 67 bytes and at most 4096'. (2) `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=300 -run TestClipBounded -cpu 1,4 ./internal/config/convert/ ./internal/config/defaults/` failed once in defaults: 'scalar_test.go:123: ... allocating 5960'. (3) A stress run, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=20 -shuffle=on -cpu 1,4 -run 'TestRunPanic|TestRunLongKeyMemory|TestKeeperTiedLongPaths|TestClipBounded|TestRunYields|TestRunCap|TestYieldGapBytes|TestScale' ./internal/config/defaults/ ./internal/config/convert/`, failed in convert with 'allocating 5848' (shuffle seed 1792236592262952846). findings.issue: Diagnostics carry unbounded content text in their paths, identities and messages. Up to 10,001 diagnostics can each repeat one long key, keyed-entry key, string set element or resource name, so the text and JSON output grow about 10^4 times faster than the source. diag.List.Sort (01 req 50) renders Path.String() on every comparison that ties on location and code, and all RZ-CFG-010 or RZ-CFG-013 diagnostics of one scalar tie, so the sort takes minutes. config/canonical (WP-39) clips member names, keyed keys and string set elements in paths and shows clipped resource names (boundElem, shown). WP-36's own meter.go docs claim the same bounding, but WP-36 bounds only messages and composite set elements. Measured with go test -overlay probes (not in the repository): (1) subst: a Route with metadata.annotations {"<4 MiB of k>": "${U0}${U1}...${U9999}"} (source about 4.27 MB) and New(Options{Schemas}).Apply gives 10,000 RZ-CFG-010 diagnostics. Each Path holds the whole 4 MiB key, the text form sums to 41,944,038,890 bytes (9,816 times the source), and diag.List.Sort took 4m19.8s (1m30.5s with a 1 MiB key, 0.10s with a 1 KiB key). (2) overlay: a base Policy of type plugin and an overlay spec.config {"<4 MiB key>": {a0: {$patch: 1}, ..., a9999: {$patch: 1}}} give 10,000 RZ-CFG-005 diagnostics, all carrying the whole key; one text line is 4,194,496 bytes and the text form is about 41.9 GB. (3) subst, each class member reproduced with 1 MiB of text and 100 undefined variables: a Consumer spec.tags string element, a Route spec.match.headers entry name, and a Route whose metadata.name is 1 MiB. Each diagnostic's path element or Resource.Name was at least 1,048,576 bytes, and one text line was about 1,049,000 bytes. Stage C does not bound metadata.name length (01 req 16 to 18), so tree.ID.Name reaches both stages unbounded. The subst RZ-CFG-007 message is built as "no schema for " + Kind + " in apiVersion " + APIVersion, unquoted and unclipped, and its path is always apiVersion, even when the apiVersion is served and the kind is the unserved part. Overlay quotes and clips both values and separates the two cases. Probe TestProbeNoSchemaMessage (`go test -count=1 -overlay /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ruralz/758d7ca3-81cf-5fbc-a967-12d97bce3d6b/scratchpad/wp36r2int/subo.json -run TestProbeNoSchemaMessage -v ./internal/config/subst/`): a 302-byte apiVersion holding a newline gives a 336-byte message with the raw text, and a served apiVersion with a 305-byte kind gives a 349-byte message at path apiVersion. Stage C drops such documents first, so only direct callers reach the RZ-CFG-007 case.

In subst's no-schema branch, do what overlay does. When the apiVersion has no index, report "apiVersion %q is not served" at the apiVersion position with path apiVersion. Otherwise report "kind %q is not served by apiVersion %q" at the kind position with path kind. Apply strconv.Quote(clip(...)) to both values. Correct the overlay/meter.go and subst/meter.go doc comments. Add one test row per class member (long key at any depth, long keyed-entry key, long string set element in subst, long resource name, long apiVersion, long kind, and a value with a newline) that asserts a bound on the summed AppendText length of the diagnostics, independent of content size. Run each row against the unfixed code. findings.issue: The new metamorphic property in FuzzOverlay is false, so the fuzz target fails on valid inputs. It says that removing an overlay member whose value is a null tree over a base scalar changes neither the result nor the diagnostics. Three input classes break it. Each pair below, added as a seed in an overlay copy of fuzz_test.go and run with `go test -count=1 -run FuzzOverlay -overlay <ov.json> ./internal/config/overlay/`, failed with "a member holding nothing but removals over a base scalar changed the merge". (a) A $patch key inside the null tree. nullTree treats `{"$patch":null}` as a removal, but the merge correctly reports a misplaced directive (RZ-CFG-005, 01 req 25). Base `{"kind":"Route","spec":{"timeout":"5s"}}` with overlay `{"spec":{"timeout":{"$patch":null}}}` gives `[RZ-CFG-005 Route/x spec.timeout.$patch]` before the drop and `[]` after it. The nested form `{"spec":{"timeout":{"x":{"$patch":null}}}}` and the dispatch member `{"spec":{"type":{"$patch":null}}}` over a cors Policy fail the same way. (b) The patch annotation inside the dropped value. The path skip matches only the member `metadata.annotations["ruralz.io/patch"]` itself, not a parent that holds it. Base `{"kind":"Route","metadata":{"annotations":"x"}}` with overlay `{"metadata":{"annotations":{"ruralz.io/patch":null}}}` loses `RZ-CFG-005 unsupported ruralz.io/patch value null`. (c) A replace annotation. With ruralz.io/patch: replace, the overlay spec is kept even when it holds nothing but removals. Base `{"kind":"Route","spec":"x"}` with overlay `{"metadata":{"annotations":{"ruralz.io/patch":"replace"}},"spec":{"a":null}}` merges to `spec:{}`, but after the drop the result has no spec. In all three cases the merge follows 01 req 25 and its documented semantics; the oracle is wrong. My severity is minor, not major:
- No requirement text is broken. 01 req 53 asks for a check "between units and every 256 nodes inside a unit", and each reference is one entry, which is checked.

The defect is the false documentation in work.go, the byteUnit comment and Options.Now ("shares the processor"), plus counters that do not measure work. Two fixes are still worth doing: the 63-byte early skip, and a contract request for maxLength 63 and the pattern on the x-ruralz-ref fields.

Switching these to `[i]` therefore needs the contract request against 01 req 48 and J row 013 that the finding proposes. itemElem already falls back to `[i]` for large composite elements, the same way config/canonical does, so a fix has precedent. The intent of "never the value" is clearly broken today.
- **headerValue:** it is not a real member of this class. Its path is `set[name=<header name>].value`, which names the header, not the credential.

Severity: minor, not major. By the design's own model, a credential-shaped literal outside x-ruralz-secret is ordinary configuration. It already appears in the Bundle, the rendered Revision, diffs and /config/dump. CM line 788 and SEC "Secrets" rule 2 guarantee non-appearance only for resolved secretRef values. The 01 test plan requires leak tests only for RZ-CFG-012 literals and env/file secrets, not for 013 literals. So the diagnostic repeats something already exposed. It is still a real gap against J row 013's intent and against the code's own documentation. Under the AGENTS.md quality standard it should be fixed: the keyWarning path, a test that asserts the credential is absent from AppendText and WriteJSON for each member, and the contract request for the set and keyed members.

result.note:
I reproduced every class member the finding lists, on the current code.

**Paths and identities.** Both packages copy the input's text into diagnostic paths and identities without clipping it:
- member names at any depth (subst walk and overlay merge/CheckBase)
- keyed-entry keys (both itemElem functions)
- subst string set elements (diag.Item(item.Text))
- resource names (ResourceID, and the overlay RZ-CFG-008 message via p.ID.String())

**Reachability.** These inputs reach stages D and E. Stage C checks only that apiVersion, kind and metadata.name are strings (01 req 16). The "RFC 1123 label, 1 to 63 chars" name rule and any annotation-key pattern apply only at stage F. 01 req 51 then runs stages D and E on that resource anyway.

**Size of the effect.** Up to 10,001 diagnostics per call can each repeat one key or name of several MiB, so the text and JSON output grow about 10^4 times faster than the source, inside the 64 MiB source limit. Sort time also grows with key length:
- 64 KiB key: 4.8s
- 256 KiB key: 13.3s

I did not rerun the finding's 4 MiB case. At that size the 41.9 GB text figure follows from the same arithmetic, and minutes of sort time is consistent with the measured trend.

**Memory.** Memory is not amplified, because the strings are substrings of the tree's text. They do keep that text alive, though; canonical's clip uses strings.Clone for exactly this reason.

**Spec status.** No 01 requirement explicitly mandates clipping path elements, and I found no documented deviation, owner decision or filed contract request that accepts the behavior. The sibling stage (canonical, WP-39) bounds the same element kinds. The subst doc at meter.go:43 says "message text quoted from the input is clipped (clip)". That is directly false for the RZ-CFG-007 no-schema message: 336 bytes from a 302-byte apiVersion, raw and unquoted, while overlay quotes and clips the same values. That branch also always reports at path apiVersion, even when the apiVersion is served and the kind is what is unserved. Stage C drops such documents first, so only direct callers reach it.

**Severity: major, not blocker.** The loader that sorts and prints diagnostics does not exist yet, and the input is an operator-authored Bundle. It is still a real amplification of cost in a pipeline whose spec bounds cost (01 req 6, 50, 54; risk 1).

**Fix location.** Clipping where WP-36 builds its diagnostics is the necessary fix. An element-wise Sort contract request against internal/config/diag is a sensible addition, but on its own it would still compare multi-MiB equal strings on every comparison.

Confirmed: the bug is in the oracle, and the merge is correct in all three classes. Spec 01 req 25 says "`$patch` in any other place, with any other value ... RZ-CFG-005". That covers A1-A3, where {"$patch":null} sits inside an object at any depth, including spec.type. The same requirement says "`ruralz.io/patch` ... any other value is RZ-CFG-005", which covers B, the null annotation value. It also says "`ruralz.io/patch: replace` replaces the base `spec` whole while `metadata` still merges". In C the base spec is not used at all, so a rule about removals over a base scalar cannot hold. The overlay's {"a":null} becomes spec {}, while dropping the member removes spec entirely.

The root cause is in two helpers in internal/config/overlay/fuzz_test.go. nullTree (lines 259-270) counts a $patch member with value null as a removal. dropRemovals (lines 232-256) skips only the exact path metadata.annotations["ruralz.io/patch"], not a parent that holds it, and ignores the replace annotation on the overlay root. The fix suggested in the finding covers all three classes:
- nullTree returns false for any $patch key at any depth.
- dropRemovals skips any subtree that holds the ruralz.io/patch key.
- dropRemovals skips the walk under spec when the overlay root carries ruralz.io/patch: replace.
The five pairs above should be added as regression seeds; with my overlay each of them fails on the current code.

Severity is minor, not major:
- Only test code is affected, and product behavior follows 01 req 25.
- `go test ./internal/config/overlay/` passes today.
- The harm is a false-positive failure in the 15-minute nightly fuzz job (stage 11), which these inputs are a few bytes away from reaching.
- A false positive cannot hide a real defect.
Under the AGENTS.md quality standard it still has to be fixed before WP-36 can close.

I modified no repository files and did not run -fuzz, because a failure there would write testdata/fuzz into the package directory.

result.summary:
WP-39 round 5 (internal/config/canonical). I fixed all four verified findings and the six minor findings, and gave every class member its own test. Before I changed any code, every finding reproduced on the snapshot (scratchpad wp39r5/orig). The working tree held no partial round-5 edits: the files were last changed at 02:xx, and the verifications ran at 08:xx.

BLOCKER: flaky goroutine bound in TestDecodeWorkersClamped.
- The test no longer reads runtime.NumGoroutine; it counts exactly. `run` now records the goroutines it started, the chunks it handed over, and the chunks in flight (inFlight and peak, written by `busy`). A tracking context records each distinct worker goroutine that calls Err.
- TestDecodeWorkersClamped (workers_test.go) asserts:
  - the trees equal those of one worker;
  - started <= min(Workers-1, handed);
  - distinct workers <= started;
  - handed <= 9;
  - peak <= 2(Workers-1)+1, and in flight is 0 at the end.

MAJOR: no yield in stage L.
- New yield.go:
  - Options and DecoderOptions get `Now func() time.Time` and `YieldAfter` (DefaultYieldAfter is 100 µs).
  - Each goroutine of a call has its own timer. The timer reads the clock at every boundary between units, and once every 256 units inside a unit. It calls runtime.Gosched once YieldAfter has passed.
  - The first read starts the interval, so the clock is read only inside work whose panics the call already recovers.
- Class members, each its own site:
  - encode: items collected in Encode and in EncodeResources; in order(), kinds checked, sortedness comparisons, sort comparisons and the duplicate check; the boundary between resources (inline and pooled; each pooled goroutine has its own timer); writer.value (also inside since defaults and the decoder's re-encoding); the boundary between chunks joined; the SHA-256, hashed in 64 KiB pieces.
  - decode: the content copy, made in pieces; parser.node; tokens in skip (shallow values and ReadDump's scan); the boundary between elements; the checker's boundary between resources (the inline checker shares the caller's timer, each worker has its own); members judged in resource(); newer-walk members and list items; keeper offers, sort comparisons and list entries; envelope document members; the two chunk loops; sequence; envelopes; scanDump members; Verify's and ReadDump's hash.
- AppendDump takes no clock: it runs on an admin request's goroutine.
- A panic in Now surfaces the same way as a panic in the work that read the clock.
- doc.go (Concurrency) and the Options and DecoderOptions docs describe this.

MAJOR: a failing decode kept memory alive.
- Class members fixed:
  - stale links in p.items and p.members after a container is copied out: now cleared;
  - scratch wider than 4,096 slots: dropped at element boundaries;
  - newerWalk frames: cleared after each resource;
  - entries of chunks checked before a finding was known (several workers): now unlinked and dropped at the parser's next chunk (`sweep`). This class member was not named in the finding; I found it while measuring.
- Not fixable here: jsonval's name records for the widest object (contract request). The test measures them apart.
- The element in flight is still built in full (part b of the finding). I did not change that code. It is documented, pinned by TestDecodeInFlightBounded (at most 250 bytes per value of MaxValues), and filed as a contract request.
- doc.go (Memory) and the MaxValues doc now state the real bounds.

MAJOR: the queue and goroutine bounds were untested.
- TestDecodeGoroutineAndQueueBounds covers Workers 2, 3 and 8 on 3,000 Routes (93 chunks).
- It runs once held: workers are kept in Err until the parse ends, and the parser yields after each element, so the bounds are reached exactly. Then it runs five times free-running.
- One worker means no goroutines and at most one chunk in flight.
- Workers-3 rows were added to TestDecodeFailingLiveHeap.

MINORS:
1. Benchmarks now use the PBB ladder pbbBundle(R) for R = 100, 1,000, 5,000 and 10,000 (116, 1,151, 5,751 and 11,501 resources), with exact and template paths, auth.jwt and ratelimit on the Gateway, and authz.cel on one Route in 20. New BenchmarkSum. Verify misses the 25 ms target: contract request.
2. doc.go now states that the trees take 12.8 times the content against the 4x target: contract request.
3. Since omission is linear. Each value is written once and taken back when it equals its default. Default bytes are memoized per writer and schema node. TestSinceLinear covers it, including defaults nested in defaults.
4. A nil index now fails Decode, Verify and ReadDump with ErrNoIndex before any read or hash.
5. posOf keeps the file when the line or column is out of range.
6. TestStageGRoundTrip runs the real stage G on Decode output (shop, shop-json and minimal; 1 and 4 workers): same bytes and digest, RoleCanonical start file, empty Source.File.

The fuzz target FuzzDecodeCanonical now also checks that yielding never changes the outcome or the re-encoding.

contractRequests: internal/jsonval (WP-02 owner): Scanner.nameSet keeps the name records of the widest object it has read until Reset. close() truncates ns.recs to base but keeps the capacity, so after an object of N members the scanner holds about 40*N bytes for the rest of the scan (2^20 members: 43 MB, 2^18: 11 MB), and a canonical decode of a hostile dump holds them for the whole parse. Change: in nameSet.close(), after `ns.recs = ns.recs[:base]`, add `if cap(ns.recs) > maxScratchNames && base <= maxScratchNames { ns.recs = append([]nameRec(nil), ns.recs...) }`, which copies at most maxScratchNames records of the objects still open. Add a jsonval test that scans an object of 2^18 members followed by more content and asserts that cap(recs) <= maxScratchNames once the object closes. Verified with an overlay of this exact change: TestDecodeFailingLiveHeap's wide-object rows drop from 43.5 MB to 165 KB held. Until then canonical's test measures the scanner apart (scannerKeeps) and does not charge it to the decoder.

Owner decision, spec 02 req 78, docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md section Validation and diff semantics (line 876) and architecture R-47. Measured: a Node loading canonical content holds trees plus their shared content copy of 12.8x the canonical size (PBB 5,000 Routes: 19.5 MB beside 1,525,363 bytes; 1,000 Routes: 13.1x; 10,000 Routes: 12.8x), and Verify allocates 14.6x, all before stages F to M run. The target is peak validation memory under 4x the canonical size. Cause: R-47 fixes Decode's result as []tree.Resource, and a WP-01 tree.Node takes 112 bytes per JSON value. Options: (a) relax the target for Node canonical loads, for example to 16x; (b) a compact decoded representation (a smaller tree.Node, or FromResources consuming a stream); (c) accept the miss and record it as an OQ row in 02 section 9. canonical/doc.go (Memory) states the figure until the owner decides.

Owner decision, spec 02 req 77 and 02 section 6 Benchmarks: 'Decoder.Verify on the 5,751-resource Revision within the 25 ms verify budget' is missed with the Node's worker count. On the PBB ladder Revision (5,751 resources, 1,525,363 bytes) at load average 2 on 4 vCPU: 30.6 ms with 1 worker, 25.8 ms with 2 (the Node's W = GOMAXPROCS/2), 23.4 ms with 4. The CPU profile is flat: parse about 32%, GC about 25%, newer walk about 13%, re-encoding about 11%, sha256 about 5%. PBB's Hot Reload stage table defines `verify` as 'Full sha256 digest and signature check' (BenchmarkSum: 1.0 ms for this Revision) and puts 'Decode and re-validate' in `compile` (400 ms). Proposed text: 02 req 77 'verification in `verify` (25 ms or less for 5,000 Routes)' becomes 'the digest check of Decoder.Verify (02 req 31(a)) counts in `verify` (25 ms or less for 5,000 Routes, PBB); decoding and the re-encoding check (02 req 31(b)) count in `compile`'. 02 section 6 becomes '`Decoder.Verify` on the 5,751-resource Revision (stage `compile`)'. The alternative is to accept and record the miss.

Owner decision, update of the WP-39 limits request (02 sections 2.6 and 9, 10 section 4): add the one-large-element shape. A decode known to fail still builds its element in flight in full before checking it, so one wide element of a hostile /config/dump costs its tree while it is parsed: about 120 bytes per value for a list and 195 for an object (60 to 65 times the bytes of a list of zeros), bounded only by MaxValues. At the default 2^26 that is some 8 to 13 GiB. TestDecodeInFlightBounded pins at most 250 bytes per value of MaxValues. The largest PBB Revision (10,000 Routes) holds 232,531 values. Proposal: a lower MaxValues for ReadDump and for Node loads, for example 2^22 (about 0.5 to 0.8 GiB in flight, still 18 times the PBB 10,000-Route Revision), or a parse that does not build the elements of a decode already known to fail. Also decide the code for that limit (RZ-CFG-001 today).

WP-69 pipeline and architecture section 2 (canonical API block), spec 01 req 53, 04 section 7 row OQ-performance-budgets-and-benchmarking-6: canonical.Options and canonical.DecoderOptions now have `Now func() time.Time` and `YieldAfter time.Duration`. Stage L's Encode and FromResources' Verify should pass the loader's Now (clock.Real().Now) and Yield. Record in the architecture's canonical block that a zero or negative YieldAfter means DefaultYieldAfter (100 µs), unlike defaults.New and precedence.New, which reject a negative value: NewDecoder has no error return, and every other DecoderOptions field treats non-positive as its default. Also update spec 02 section 3's canonical API block, which still shows NewDecoder(idx, *hub.Normalizer) and Decode(content) (*hub.Bundle, error), to the implemented API: NewDecoder(idx, DecoderOptions); Decode, Verify and ReadDump taking ctx and Source and returning []tree.Resource; Options{Level, Workers, Now, YieldAfter}.

internal/config/revision (WP-01 owner), optional: add `func FromSum(sum [sha256.Size]byte) Digest`, or an incremental hasher returning a Digest. Canonical hashes large Revisions in 64 KiB pieces with a yield read between pieces (yield.go `sum`) and today builds the Digest by formatting the SHA-256 as hex and calling revision.Parse, which cannot fail on that input.
deviations: The sixth minor finding reached me cut off ('...but nothing pins this at t'). From the visible text (02 test plan item 13, Materialize(Decode(x)) == Decode(x), R-47 RoleCanonical and Source.Files), I added TestStageGRoundTrip, which runs the real defaults stage on Verify output. The mutant that registers the decoded file as RoleBase kills it. Any part of that finding past the cut was not visible to me.

Negative YieldAfter means DefaultYieldAfter in both Options and DecoderOptions. The fix suggested 'negative handled as in defaults/precedence', where it is an error. NewDecoder has no error return, and every other DecoderOptions field treats non-positive as its default. I filed this for the architecture in a contract request; I did not change the constructor signature.

Part (b) of the memory major (the element in flight is built in full even when the decode is already known to fail) is not removed in code, as that finding's own fix asks: docs (doc.go Memory and the MaxValues doc), a bound test (TestDecodeInFlightBounded, at most 250 bytes per value of MaxValues), and the limits contract request with the one-large-element shape. Removing it would need a parse that walks newer fields without building trees, which is a redesign of the decoder.

Behavior change: once a finding is known, a decode now drops the entries (trees) of chunks it had already checked, at the parser's next chunk (`sweep`). Two tests changed to match. TestDecodeRetention's row 'a newer field at resource 50' now expects 0 kept entries instead of 50, and gained a form-finding row. TestCheckerSkips now checks for skipped re-encoding by the values the re-encoding wrote (yield site counts), because a failing decode keeps no entries to inspect. chunk.checked became run.checked for the same reason.

Test-only state in production types: Encoder and Decoder have an unexported `observe` hook that is nil outside tests. `yielder` keeps per-site counters, checks and yields. `run` keeps started, handed, inFlight, peak and checked. Each costs a nil check or an atomic add per chunk or element. They are what let the tests count goroutines, queue depth and yields exactly instead of sampling runtime.NumGoroutine.

Not divided by yields, as documented in doc.go Concurrency: a single token scanned by jsonval, the io.ReadAll of a /config/dump body (the reader's I/O; ReadDump is CLI-only in M1), one schemaidx call for one value (for example ItemElem of a large set element, only on a finding), append growth of an encode buffer, and AppendDump, which runs on an admin request's goroutine and takes no clock.

TestDecodeFailingLiveHeap reads 4 MiB of short elements with one worker but a sixteenth of that with three, and the wide rows hold 2^18 values rather than 2^20. With three workers the measure must inspect the stack on every context call, which made the race suite approach the 10-minute timeout. The one-worker rows keep the sizes the old fixes were proven with, and every new row fails on the old code at these sizes (8 to 46 MB held against the 1 MiB bound).
